v3 adds that formula as an explicit prerequisite with an independent Lean contract and a complete proof: the new child carrier_area_formula (`idtp_carrier_area_formula`, Simon Ch. 3, 2.4–2.5).
- Hypotheses: n ≥ 1; M Borel, countably n-rectifiable and locally H^n-finite; Z open; F C¹ on Z into ℝ^n; h a.e. measurable for H^n⌞M.
- Conclusion: the fibre-sum function is a.e. measurable, and ∫ Σ_{x∈M∩Z∩F⁻¹(y)} h(x) dy = ∫_{M∩Z} J*·h dH^n, where J* is the Gram-determinant Jacobian of F along approxTangentPlane n M x.

The proof covers each item the audit listed:
- Rectifiable parametrization reduction (step 2): disjoint Borel bi-Lipschitz pieces g_i(A_i), built with SimonGMT areaRegularSet / area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero, Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt and Lusin–Souslin.

- Null-set handling (steps 0, 1(c), 4, 7): locally Lipschitz images of H^n-null sets are L^n-null, and a.e.-measurable weights reduce to Borel ones.
- Transfer of parameter fibre sums to carrier fibre sums (steps 6–7): SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_fiberSum on the fibre side and weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn (arbitrary weights) on the carrier side.

subproblems.title: Mass bounds pass to ConvergesWeakly-limits of currents on varying domains
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, all sets U_j ⊆ ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) and V ⊆ ℝ^P, all currents T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(V), every set W ⊆ ℝ^P and every B ∈ [0, ∞]: if T_j ⇀ S in the sense of ConvergesWeakly (currentEval(T_j, ω) → S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V)) and, for all sufficiently large j, W ⊆ U_j and M_W(T_j) ≤ B, then M_W(S) ≤ B. Here M_W = massOn is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over test forms ω of the current's domain with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm ≤ 1 everywhere.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (B : ℝ≥0∞), ConvergesWeakly Ts S → (∀ᶠ j in atTop, W ⊆ Us j ∧ (Ts j).massOn W ≤ B) → S.massOn W ≤ B
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence, Simon 6.2.14 (SimonGMT `WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf`, Chapter06/Mass.lean:100), in the varying-domain form used by the parent proof (step 3: "S(ω) = lim currentEval(blowUp T x_i λ_i, ω) ≤ liminf M_{B_ρ(w)}(blowUp T x_i λ_i)"; step 5(d) for members with λ = 0; step 5(e) for the cones C; step 8 for the support of a tangent cone).
1. By definition M_W(S) = S.massOn W is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(S(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn V n W, i.e. over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for every x. Hence it suffices to fix such an ω and to prove ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ B.
2. By hypothesis there is j₀ such that W ⊆ U_j and M_W(T_j) ≤ B for every j ≥ j₀. Let j ≥ j₀. The differential form ω is a test form (smooth with compact support, because ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V)) and tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ U_j, so the same form defines an element ω_j ∈ 𝒟^n(U_j), and by the definition of currentEval, currentEval(T_j, ω) = T_j(ω_j). The form ω_j has the same support and the same pointwise coefficient norms as ω, so ω_j ∈ massAdmissibleOn U_j n W and ofReal(T_j(ω_j)) ≤ M_W(T_j) ≤ B (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Thus ofReal(currentEval(T_j, ω)) ≤ B for every j ≥ j₀.
3. By ConvergesWeakly, currentEval(T_j, ω) → S(ω) in ℝ, and ENNReal.ofReal is continuous, so ofReal(currentEval(T_j, ω)) → ofReal(S(ω)) in [0, ∞]. The set {t ∈ [0, ∞] : t ≤ B} is closed and contains the terms with j ≥ j₀, hence it contains the limit: ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ B.
4. Since ω was an arbitrary admissible form, M_W(S) = sup ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ B. ∎
proof_key_steps: M_W(S) is the supremum of ofReal(S(ω)) over massAdmissibleOn V n W, so fix one admissible ω.
For j ≥ j₀, tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ U_j, so currentEval(T_j, ω) = T_j(ω) with ω admissible for M_W(T_j); hence ofReal(currentEval(T_j, ω)) ≤ M_W(T_j) ≤ B.
ConvergesWeakly and continuity of ofReal give ofReal(currentEval(T_j, ω)) → ofReal(S(ω)); the closed set {t ≤ B} contains the limit.
Take the supremum over admissible ω.

subproblems.title: The density of an integer multiplicity measure equals its multiplicity H^n-almost everywhere
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P and every integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U n (carrier M, multiplicity θ : ℝ^P → ℕ, orientation ξ), if the measure μ_R := R.measure = θ·μHE[n]⌞M satisfies μ_R(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, then for μHE[n]-almost every x ∈ ℝ^P the ratio μ_R(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) (open balls, ω_n = unitBallVolume n, computed in [0, ∞]) tends to 1_M(x)·θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), 1 ≤ n → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → R.measure K ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => R.measure (ball x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (Set.indicator R.carrier (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ≥0∞)) x))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remarks 1.8(1),(2) and Theorem 1.9 (density of θH^n⌞M equals θ H^n-a.e. on a countably n-rectifiable M) and Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2) (upper density theorem), which the parent proof cites in step 3 ("Θ_S equals the multiplicity of S μ_S-a.e.") and in step 5(iii) ("μ_A = ϑ_A·H^n"). Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, H^n := μHE[n], ν := H^n⌞M, μ := R.measure = θ·ν; for a Borel measure λ on ℝ^P and x ∈ ℝ^P put D(λ, x) := limsup_{ρ↓0} λ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) ∈ [0, ∞] (open balls; closed balls give the same value because B_ρ ⊆ B̄_ρ ⊆ B_{ρ(1+ε)}).
1. (Local finiteness.) θ ≥ 1 on M (mult_pos, ℕ-valued), so ν(K) ≤ μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. Thus ν and μ are locally finite Borel measures on ℝ^P (hence Radon and σ-finite, ℝ^P being σ-compact), and θ ∈ L¹_loc(ν) because ∫_K θ dν = μ(K) < ∞.
2. (Upper density theorem.) If λ is a locally finite Borel measure on ℝ^P and A ⊆ ℝ^P is Borel, then D(λ⌞A, x) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ A. This is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 (for λ(A) < ∞) together with Remark 3.7(2) (cover ℝ^P by the open balls B_j(0), each of finite λ-measure); in the library it is SimonGMT `ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside_of_openSigmaFinite` (Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean), stated for the Borel regular outer measure λ (open-σ-finite because λ is locally finite), with closed-ball density quotients, and almost everywhere with respect to Simon's normalized Hausdorff measure `simonHausdorffMeasureReal n`, a positive constant multiple of μH[n]; closed and open balls give the same upper density, and the null sets of `simonHausdorffMeasureReal n`, μH[n] and μHE[n] coincide. [Proof sketch, Simon 1.3.3: for t > 0 and closed C ⊆ A, every x ∈ S_t := {x ∉ A : D(λ⌞A, x) ≥ t} satisfies D(λ⌞(A ∖ C), x) ≥ t, so the Vitali covering argument gives t·H^n(S_t) ≤ λ(A ∖ C), and λ(A ∖ C) can be made arbitrarily small.]
3. (Off M.) μ = μ⌞M, so by (2) with λ := μ and A := M, D(μ, x) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ M. At every such x the nonnegative ratio μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) has limsup 0, hence tends to 0 = 1_M(x)θ(x).
4. (Lusin decomposition, Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1).) By Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17) applied to the measurable function θ and the locally finite measure ν, there are compact sets M_1 ⊆ M_2 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ M with θ|M_j continuous and ν(M ∖ ∪_jM_j) = 0. By (2) with A := M ∖ M_j and λ := ν, resp. λ := μ: D(ν⌞(M ∖ M_j), x) = 0 and D(μ⌞(M ∖ M_j), x) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M_j.
5. (Approximate tangent planes.) By the field `orients` of the structure IMRep, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M there is an n-dimensional subspace Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x, i.e. ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_{Q_x} f dH^n as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) (these integrals are those of the locally finite measures H^n⌞η_{x,r}(M), by (1) and scaling). Let G be the set of x ∈ M such that x has such a Q_x, x ∈ M_j for some j, and the two upper densities in (4) vanish at x for every j with x ∈ M_j; by (4), (5) and ν(M ∖ ∪M_j) = 0, H^n(M ∖ G) = 0.
6. (Density of ν at x ∈ G.) H^n(η_{x,ρ}(A)) = ρ^{−n}H^n(A) for every A (homothety scaling of μHE[n], Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image`), so ν(B_ρ(x))/ρ^n = H^n(η_{x,ρ}(M) ∩ B_1(0)). For ε ∈ (0, 1) choose continuous f, g : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with compact support and 1_{B_{1−ε}(0)} ≤ f ≤ 1_{B_1(0)} ≤ g ≤ 1_{B_{1+ε}(0)}. Then ∫_{Q_x} f dH^n ≤ liminf_{ρ↓0} H^n(η_{x,ρ}(M) ∩ B_1(0)) ≤ limsup_{ρ↓0} H^n(η_{x,ρ}(M) ∩ B_1(0)) ≤ ∫_{Q_x} g dH^n, and H^n(Q_x ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_ns^n (μHE[n] on the n-dimensional subspace Q_x is the image of Lebesgue measure of ℝ^n under a linear isometry; Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). So ω_n(1 − ε)^n ≤ liminf ≤ limsup ≤ ω_n(1 + ε)^n for every ε, i.e. ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1. (The scaling of μHE[n] under dilations used here is the accepted `Submission.dtc_hausdorff_dilation`, which may be reused.)
7. (Density of μ at x ∈ G.) Let x ∈ G ∩ M_j. Then μ(B_ρ(x)) = ∫_{M_j ∩ B_ρ(x)} θ dH^n + μ⌞(M ∖ M_j)(B_ρ(x)). The second term is o(ρ^n) because D(μ⌞(M ∖ M_j), x) = 0. Given ε > 0, continuity of θ|M_j at x gives |θ(y) − θ(x)| ≤ ε for y ∈ M_j ∩ B_ρ(x) and small ρ, so the first term lies between (θ(x) − ε)ν(M_j ∩ B_ρ(x)) and (θ(x) + ε)ν(M_j ∩ B_ρ(x)); and ν(M_j ∩ B_ρ(x)) = ν(B_ρ(x)) − ν⌞(M ∖ M_j)(B_ρ(x)) = ω_nρ^n(1 + o(1)) by (6) and D(ν⌞(M ∖ M_j), x) = 0. Hence θ(x) − ε ≤ liminf μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) ≤ limsup ≤ θ(x) + ε for every ε > 0, so μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → θ(x) = 1_M(x)θ(x).
8. (Conclusion.) The exceptional set is contained in the union of the H^n-null sets of (3) and of M ∖ G, so the ratio μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) tends to 1_M(x)θ(x) in [0, ∞] for μHE[n]-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν := μHE[n]⌞M ≤ μ_R, so ν and μ_R are locally finite and θ ∈ L¹_loc(ν).
Upper density theorem (Simon 1.3.6, 1.3.7(2)): the upper density of λ⌞A vanishes H^n-a.e. off A.
Off M the density of μ_R is 0 H^n-a.e.
Lusin: compact M_j ⊆ M with θ|M_j continuous exhaust M up to a ν-null set; the upper densities of ν⌞(M∖M_j), μ_R⌞(M∖M_j) vanish H^n-a.e. on M_j.
At points with an approximate tangent plane (field `orients`), ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1, by homothety scaling and continuous cutoffs.
Continuity of θ on M_j gives μ_R(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → θ(x) H^n-a.e. on M.

subproblems.title: Constancy theorem for integer multiplicity cycles supported in an n-plane: S = c[[Q]] and M_W(S) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, every open V ⊆ ℝ^P, every orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P with Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}, and every S ∈ 𝒟_n(V): if S is integer multiplicity, ∂S = 0 in V (BoundaryVanishes S), spt S ⊆ Q and V ∩ Q is connected (in particular nonempty), then there is c ∈ ℤ such that S(ω) = c·∫_{V∩Q} ω(x)(τ_1, …, τ_n) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V) (S = c[[Q]] in V, with Q oriented by τ), and M_W(S) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ V. Here H^n = μHE[n] and |c| = c.natAbs.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), 1 ≤ n → IsOpen V → Orthonormal ℝ τ → IsIntegerMultiplicity S → BoundaryVanishes S → S.support ⊆ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)) → IsConnected (V ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P))) → ∃ c : ℤ, (∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, S ω = (c : ℝ) * ∫ x in V ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x τ ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ V → S.massOn W = (c.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[n] (W ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the Constancy Theorem, Simon Ch. 6, Theorem 2.34 (and its use for currents carried by a plane in the proof of the deformation theorem, Simon Ch. 6, (26)–(27)), cited by the parent proof in step 4 ("by the constancy theorem (Ch. 6, 2.34) on the connected sets P_i ∖ {0}") and in step 8 ("By constancy (∂C = 0, C integer multiplicity, Π connected), C = c₀[[Π]]"). This version records both conclusions of the theorem: the current identity S = c[[Q]] (used for tangent cones by the sibling children cone_tangent_cone_planar and cone_sector_endpoint_density) and the mass identity. Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an integer multiplicity current, the conventions of im_mass_measure (`Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure`) are used. Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}; τ is orthonormal, hence a basis of Q, and dim Q = n.
1. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep V n represent S and μ := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M. By im_mass_measure (a), M_W(S) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ V; by (b), a point x ∈ V lies outside spt S iff μ(B_ε(x)) = 0 for some ε > 0.
2. μ(V ∖ Q) = 0 and H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0: V ∖ Q is open (Q is closed) and disjoint from spt S, so each of its points has a μ-null ball; by Lindelöf (ℝ^P is second countable) countably many such balls cover V ∖ Q. As M ⊆ V and θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∖ Q) ≤ μ(M ∖ Q) = 0.
3. Use the given orthonormal basis τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) of Q, the linear isometry ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, ι(s) = Σ_i s_iτ_i (image Q), and ξ_Q ∈ Λ_n given by ξ_Q(α) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n). Then H^n⌞Q = ι_#(L^n) (μHE[n] is preserved by isometries and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n; Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`).
4. (Orientation.) By the field `orients`, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ Q there is an n-dimensional Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and ξ(x) = ±(α ↦ α(τ'_x)) for an orthonormal basis τ'_x of Q_x. We claim Q_x = Q. Since H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0, ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M ∩ Q)} f dH^n (H^n(η_{x,r}(M ∖ Q)) = r^{−n}H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0), and η_{x,r}(M ∩ Q) ⊆ Q because x ∈ Q and Q is a subspace. So ∫_{Q_x} f dH^n = 0 for every continuous compactly supported f ≥ 0 vanishing on Q. If Q_x ≠ Q, then Q_x ∩ Q is a proper subspace of Q_x and Q_x ∖ Q contains a nonempty relatively open subset of Q_x, on which a suitable such f is positive; its H^n⌞Q_x-integral is positive, a contradiction. Hence Q_x = Q. Two orthonormal bases of Q differ by an orthogonal matrix A, and α(τ'_x) = det(A)·α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating n-form α. Therefore ξ(x) = ε(x)ξ_Q with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1} for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ Q; ε = ξ(·)(α₀) for any fixed α₀ with α₀(τ) = 1 is H^n⌞M-measurable (ξ is a.e. strongly measurable).
5. Put g := 1_M·ε·θ on Q, an integer-valued H^n⌞Q-measurable function with ∫_{K ∩ Q}|g| dH^n ≤ μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ V. By (2) and (4), for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V), S(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n = ∫_{V ∩ Q} g(x)⟨ω(x), ξ_Q⟩ dH^n(x), and μ = |g|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q).
6. (Zero weak derivatives.) Let Ω := ι^{−1}(V) ⊆ ℝ^n (open; ι restricts to a homeomorphism of Ω onto V ∩ Q, so Ω is connected and nonempty) and h := g∘ι ∈ L¹_loc(Ω). Let ψ ∈ C^∞_c(Ω) and i ∈ {1, …, n}. Since ι(spt ψ) is a compact subset of the open set V, there is δ > 0 with {y ∈ ℝ^P : ι^*(y) ∈ spt ψ, |y − p_Q(y)| ≤ δ} ⊆ V, where ι^*(y) := (⟨y, τ_1⟩, …, ⟨y, τ_n⟩) and p_Q is the orthogonal projection onto Q. With χ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P), χ = 1 near 0, spt χ ⊆ B_δ(0), put f(y) := ψ(ι^*(y))·χ(y − p_Q(y)): f ∈ C^∞_c(V), f(ι(s)) = ψ(s) and D_{τ_i}f(ι(s)) = ∂_iψ(s) (the second factor is 1 near Q and τ_i − p_Q(τ_i) = 0). Let α_i := τ_1^♭ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_{i−1}^♭ ∧ τ_{i+1}^♭ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_n^♭ (τ_j^♭ := ⟨τ_j, ·⟩; for n = 1, α_1 := 1) and φ := f·α_i ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(V). Then dφ = df ∧ α_i and ⟨dφ(x), ξ_Q⟩ = (df ∧ α_i)(τ_1, …, τ_n) = (−1)^{i−1}D_{τ_i}f(x). Since ∂S = 0 in V, 0 = ∂S(φ) = S(dφ) = (−1)^{i−1}∫_{V ∩ Q} g D_{τ_i}f dH^n = (−1)^{i−1}∫_Ω h(s)∂_iψ(s) ds by (3) and (5).
7. (Constancy.) A function h ∈ L¹_loc(Ω) all of whose weak first derivatives vanish on the connected open set Ω ⊆ ℝ^n is a.e. equal to a constant c: the mollifications h_ε := h ∗ φ_ε are smooth with ∇h_ε = 0 on {s : dist(s, ∂Ω) > ε}, hence locally constant there, and h_ε → h in L¹_loc(Ω), so h is a.e. constant near every point, and connectedness makes the constant global (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 2.34; SimonGMT `WeakDerivativesZero.ae_eq_const`, `ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero`, Chapter08/DistributionalConstancy.lean). (If a library form of this fact tests against C¹_c functions, note that (6) extends from ψ ∈ C^∞_c(Ω) to ψ ∈ C¹_c(Ω): the mollifications ψ_ε ∈ C^∞_c(Ω) have supports in a fixed compact subset K of Ω for small ε and ∂_iψ_ε → ∂_iψ uniformly, while h is integrable on K, so ∫_Ω h∂_iψ = lim ∫_Ω h∂_iψ_ε = 0.) Since h takes integer values and h = c on a set of positive measure (Ω is open and nonempty), c ∈ ℤ.
8. (Conclusion.) By (7), h = c L^n-a.e. on Ω; since ι maps L^n-null subsets of Ω onto H^n-null subsets of V ∩ Q (by (3)), g = c H^n-a.e. on V ∩ Q. Hence, by (5), for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V), S(ω) = ∫_{V∩Q} c⟨ω(x), ξ_Q⟩ dH^n(x) = c·∫_{V∩Q} ω(x)(τ_1, …, τ_n) dH^n(x), which is the current identity. Also μ = |g|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q) = |c|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q), so for every open W ⊆ V, M_W(S) = μ(W) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ V ∩ Q) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q), with |c| = c.natAbs. ∎
proof_key_steps: Represent S by R = (M, θ, ξ); M_W(S) = R.measure(W) on open W ⊆ V and spt S is the support of R.measure in V.
spt S ⊆ Q gives R.measure(V ∖ Q) = 0 (Lindelöf), so H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0.
A.e. on M the approximate tangent plane is Q, so ξ = ±ξ_Q with ξ_Q(α) = α(τ), and S(ω) = ∫_{V∩Q} g⟨ω, ξ_Q⟩ dH^n with g integer-valued and L¹_loc.
∂S = 0 tested on f·α_i (f extending ψ ∈ C^∞_c(ι^{−1}V) off Q) gives zero weak derivatives of g∘ι on the connected open ι^{−1}(V).
Distributional constancy: g = c ∈ ℤ a.e., so S(ω) = c∫_{V∩Q} ω(x)(τ) dH^n, R.measure = |c|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q) and M_W(S) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q).

subproblems.title: Weighted area formula on a countably n-rectifiable carrier for a C¹ map into ℝ^n (Simon Ch. 3, 2.4–2.5)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, every Borel set M ⊆ ℝ^P that is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable n M) with H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P (H^n := μHE[n]), every open Z ⊆ ℝ^P, every map F : ℝ^P → ℝ^n (= Euclid n) that is C¹ on Z (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F Z) and every h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] that is a.e. measurable for H^n⌞M: the fibre-sum function y ↦ Σ_{x ∈ M ∩ Z, F(x) = y} h(x) ∈ [0, ∞] (the tsum over the subtype M ∩ Z ∩ F^{−1}{y}) is a.e. measurable for Lebesgue measure L^n (volume) on ℝ^n, and ∫_{ℝ^n} Σ_{x ∈ M ∩ Z, F(x) = y} h(x) dL^n(y) = ∫_{M∩Z} J*(x)·h(x) dH^n(x), where J*(x) := (det(⟨DF(x)u_i, DF(x)u_j⟩)_{i,j})^{1/2}, DF(x) = fderiv ℝ F x and (u_i) is the standard orthonormal basis (stdOrthonormalBasis) of the approximate tangent plane T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x, indexed by Fin (dim T_x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M Z : Set (Euclid P)) (F : Euclid P → Euclid n) (h : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞), 1 ≤ n → MeasurableSet M → CountablyRectifiable n M → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μHE[n] (M ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → IsOpen Z → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F Z → AEMeasurable h (μHE[n].restrict M) → AEMeasurable (fun y : Euclid n => ∑' x : ↥(M ∩ Z ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) volume ∧ ∫⁻ y, (∑' x : ↥(M ∩ Z ∩ F ⁻¹' {y}), h x) ∂volume = ∫⁻ x in M ∩ Z, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ (approxTangentPlane n M x)) => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ F x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (approxTangentPlane n M x) i)) (fderiv ℝ F x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (approxTangentPlane n M x) j))))) * h x ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, §2, 2.1–2.6 (chapter-03.txt lines 330–407): for a countably n-rectifiable M and a locally Lipschitz f, (2.4) ∫_A J^M_f dH^n = ∫ H^0(A ∩ f^{−1}(y)) dH^n(y), and its weighted form (2.5) for nonnegative H^n-measurable h. The book proves (2.4) by decomposing M into pieces M_j ⊆ N_j of C¹ submanifolds (Lemma 1.2), identifying J^M_f on M_j with the Jacobian of a C¹ map on N_j, applying the smooth area formula (Ch. 2, 3.4) and summing over j. The present proof follows the same plan with Lipschitz-parametrized bi-Lipschitz pieces in place of C¹ submanifolds, because the library provides the verified Euclidean-domain Lipschitz area formula (SimonGMT Chapter02, Simon Ch. 2, 3.4–3.5) but neither the C¹ approximation theorem nor the C¹ cover of Lemma 1.2: step 2 is the parametrization reduction (Simon Ch. 3, 1.2–1.3), step 3 the identification of approximate tangent planes along a piece (the density argument of Simon's proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒", lines 109–143, with a bi-Lipschitz image in place of a C¹ manifold), step 5 the Jacobian chain rule, steps 0, 1(c), 4 and 7 the null-set handling, and step 7 the transfer of parameter fibre sums to carrier fibre sums. It is used with n = 2 by the sibling child cone_sector_endpoint_density (step 7). Notation. E := ℝ^P = Euclid P; ℝ^n := Euclid n with Lebesgue measure L^n := volume; H^n := μHE[n] on E or on ℝ^n, and on ℝ^n, μHE[n] = L^n (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). B_ρ(x) and B̄_ρ(x) are the open and the closed ball. For a map φ between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, Dφ(a) := fderiv ℝ φ a (the zero map where φ is not differentiable) and J_φ(a) := normDet(Dφ(a)) (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt φ a; Mathlib LinearMap.normDet, the nonnegative square root of det(Dφ(a)^*Dφ(a))). T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x and J*(x) is the integrand factor of the statement. For S ⊆ E and y ∈ ℝ^n, Σ_S(y) := Σ_{x ∈ S, F(x) = y} h(x) ∈ [0, ∞] is the tsum over the subtype S ∩ F^{−1}{y} (SimonGMT weightedAreaFiberSum S F h y); the statement concerns Σ_{M∩Z}. Library facts used. (L1) Lipschitz images. If φ : X → Y (finite-dimensional real inner product spaces) is K-Lipschitz on S ⊆ X, then H^n(φ(S)) ≤ K^n·H^n(S): Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le for μH[n], and μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with a constant c_n ∈ (0, ∞) depending only on n (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero). In particular Lipschitz images of H^n-null sets are H^n-null. (A1) Euclidean weighted area formula (SimonGMT Chapter02/AreaNoninjective.lean, weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_fiberSum and aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitz): for a Lipschitz φ : ℝ^n → Y, a Borel s ⊆ ℝ^n and a Borel w : ℝ^n → [0, ∞], the fibre sum y ↦ Σ_{a ∈ s, φ(a) = y} w(a) is μHE[n]-a.e. measurable on Y and ∫_Y Σ_{a ∈ s, φ(a) = y} w(a) dμHE[n](y) = ∫_s J_φ(a)w(a) dL^n(a) (finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n). (A2) Injective area formula (SimonGMT Chapter02/AreaLipschitz.lean, weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn): for a Lipschitz φ : ℝ^n → Y, a Borel s on which φ is injective and an arbitrary (not necessarily measurable) κ : Y → [0, ∞], ∫_{φ(s)} κ dμHE[n] = ∫_s J_φ(a)κ(φ(a)) dL^n(a). (G) Gram determinants and the chain rule (Mathlib Analysis/InnerProductSpace/NormDet.lean). For a linear A : E → ℝ^n and a subspace T ⊆ E with orthonormal basis u, det(⟨Au_i, Au_j⟩)_{i,j} = normDet(A|_T)² (LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram applied to A.domRestrict T and u); since normDet ≥ 0, J*(x) = normDet(DF(x)|_{T_x}) for every x. For linear L : ℝ^n → E and A : E → ℝ^n, normDet(A∘L) = normDet(A|_{range L})·normDet(L) (LinearMap.normDet_comp). (D) Density points. For Borel S ⊆ ℝ^n, L^n-a.e. a ∈ S is a density point of S: L^n(S ∩ B̄_ρ(a))/L^n(B̄_ρ(a)) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺ (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div). If a ∈ S is a density point and v ∈ ℝ^n, there are r_k → 0⁺ and v_k → v with a + r_kv_k ∈ S. For v = 0 take v_k := 0. For v ≠ 0 suppose not; then there are ε ∈ (0, |v|) and r_1 > 0 with S ∩ (a + rB_ε(v)) = ∅ for all r ∈ (0, r_1); as a + rB_ε(v) ⊆ B̄_{r(|v|+ε)}(a) has L^n-measure (ε/(|v| + ε))^n·L^n(B̄_{r(|v|+ε)}(a)) (Lebesgue measure scales by r^n, and open and closed balls have equal measure, Measure.addHaar_closedBall_eq_addHaar_ball, ℝ^n being nontrivial as n ≥ 1), L^n(S ∩ B̄_ρ(a))/L^n(B̄_ρ(a)) ≤ 1 − (ε/(|v| + ε))^n for all ρ ∈ (0, r_1(|v| + ε)), contradicting density.
0. (Reduction to Borel h.) As h is a.e. measurable for H^n⌞M, there is a Borel h̃ : E → [0, ∞] with (H^n⌞M)({h ≠ h̃}) = 0, i.e. H^n(N_h) = 0 for N_h := M ∩ {h ≠ h̃} (M is Borel, Measure.restrict_apply'). The right-hand sides for h and h̃ agree, since the integrands agree on (M ∩ Z) ∖ N_h. The fibre sums Σ_{M∩Z}(y) for h and for h̃ agree at every y ∉ F(N_h ∩ Z), and F(N_h ∩ Z) is L^n-null by step 1(c). So both conclusions for h follow from those for h̃ (a.e. measurability is preserved under change on a null set, and lintegrals of a.e. equal functions agree). From now on h is Borel.
1. (Lipschitz localization of F.) (a) If Z = ∅, every fibre is empty, the fibre-sum function is the constant 0 and both sides vanish; assume Z ≠ ∅. For x ∈ Z choose r_x > 0 with B̄_{r_x}(x) ⊆ Z (Z is open). F is C¹ on the convex compact set B̄_{r_x}(x), hence Lipschitz on it (Mathlib ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith). The balls B_{r_x}(x), x ∈ Z, cover Z and E is second countable, so countably many of them cover Z; enumerate them as V_0, V_1, … (repetitions allowed) and let K_l be a Lipschitz constant of F on V_l. (b) By Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension there is a Lipschitz F_l : E → ℝ^n with F_l = F on V_l. Put Z_l := V_l ∖ ∪_{l'<l} V_{l'}. The Z_l are Borel and pairwise disjoint, ∪_l Z_l = Z, and F = F_l on Z_l. (c) If S ⊆ Z and H^n(S) = 0, then F(S) = ∪_l F_l(S ∩ Z_l) is L^n-null by (L1) (μHE[n] = L^n on ℝ^n).
2. (Bi-Lipschitz pieces of M.) There are Lipschitz maps g_i : ℝ^n → E, Borel sets A_i ⊆ ℝ^n and constants c_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that: (i) c_i|a − a'| ≤ |g_i(a) − g_i(a')| for all a, a' ∈ A_i (so g_i is injective on A_i); (ii) g_i is differentiable at every a ∈ A_i and Dg_i(a) is injective; (iii) the sets g_i(A_i) are Borel subsets of M and pairwise disjoint; (iv) H^n(M ∖ ∪_i g_i(A_i)) = 0. Proof. (2a) By CountablyRectifiable n M there are M_0 ⊆ E with H^n(M_0) = 0 and Lipschitz maps G_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ∪_j G_j(ℝ^n). (2b) Let R_j := {a : G_j is differentiable at a and DG_j(a) is injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet G_j); R_j is Borel (measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and H^n(G_j(ℝ^n ∖ R_j)) = 0 (area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero with s := univ). (2c) For an injective linear A : ℝ^n → E choose m(A) > 0 with |Av| ≥ m(A)|v| for all v (m(A) := 1/K for an antilipschitz constant K > 0 of A, Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith), and put r(A) := m(A)/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise; so r(A) > 0 for every A. (2d) For each j, Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (f := G_j, s := R_j, f' := DG_j — at a ∈ R_j, G_j has derivative DG_j(a), hence also within R_j — and the radius function r) gives pairwise disjoint measurable sets t_{j,k} (k ∈ ℕ) with R_j ⊆ ∪_k t_{j,k} and continuous linear maps A_{j,k} with |G_j(a) − G_j(a') − A_{j,k}(a − a')| ≤ r(A_{j,k})|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ R_j ∩ t_{j,k}, and, if R_j ≠ ∅, A_{j,k} = DG_j(y) for some y ∈ R_j. (2e) Put D_{j,k} := R_j ∩ t_{j,k} (Borel). If D_{j,k} ≠ ∅, then A := A_{j,k} = DG_j(y) with y ∈ R_j is injective, r(A) = m(A)/2, and for a, a' ∈ D_{j,k}, |G_j(a) − G_j(a')| ≥ |A(a − a')| − (m(A)/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m(A)/2)|a − a'| = r(A_{j,k})|a − a'|. (2f) Let i ↦ (j(i), k(i)) be the bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ (Nat.unpair) and put g_i := G_{j(i)}, D_i := D_{j(i),k(i)}, c_i := r(A_{j(i),k(i)}) > 0 and N_i := g_i(D_i); N_i is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn; g_i is continuous and, by (2e), injective on D_i). (2g) Put A_i := D_i ∩ g_i^{−1}(M ∖ ∪_{i'<i} N_{i'}) (Borel). Then g_i(A_i) = (N_i ∩ M) ∖ ∪_{i'<i} N_{i'} is Borel and contained in M, and for i' < i, g_{i'}(A_{i'}) ⊆ N_{i'} is disjoint from g_i(A_i): (iii). Since A_i ⊆ D_i ⊆ R_{j(i)}, (i) holds by (2e) and (ii) by the definition of R_{j(i)}. (2h) If x ∈ M ∖ (M_0 ∪ ∪_j G_j(ℝ^n ∖ R_j)), then x = G_j(a) with a ∈ R_j ⊆ ∪_k t_{j,k}; so a ∈ D_i for the index i of the pair (j, k) and x ∈ N_i ∩ M; if i_0 is the least index with x ∈ N_{i_0}, then x ∈ g_{i_0}(A_{i_0}). Hence M ∖ ∪_i g_i(A_i) ⊆ M_0 ∪ ∪_j G_j(ℝ^n ∖ R_j), an H^n-null set: (iv).
3. (Approximate tangent planes along a piece.) For every i and L^n-a.e. a ∈ A_i, M has the approximate tangent space range Dg_i(a) at g_i(a) (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (g_i(a)) (range Dg_i(a))); consequently T_{g_i(a)} = range Dg_i(a). The "consequently": by definition approxTangentPlane n M x is a chosen Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q whenever such a Q exists, and any two such Q coincide (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Recall that HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q means dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{y,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(E), where η_{y,r}(z) := r^{−1}(z − y) (SimonGMT blowUpMap y r). Proof. Fix i and write g := g_i, B := A_i, c := c_i, Λ := a Lipschitz constant of g, Γ := g(B) ⊆ M (Borel by step 2), λ := L^n, ω_n := λ(B̄_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞) and ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f|. (3a) Preliminaries. The inverse G : Γ → B of g|_B is c^{−1}-Lipschitz, so by (L1) λ(G(N)) ≤ c^{−n}H^n(N) for N ⊆ Γ: a property holding at every point of Γ outside an H^n-null set N holds at g(b) for every b ∈ B ∖ G(N), and G(N) is λ-null. H^n(g(S)) ≤ Λ^nλ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^n (L1). For r > 0 and S ⊆ E, H^n(η_{y,r}(S)) = r^{−n}H^n(S) (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image together with the isometry invariance Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image for the translation z ↦ z − y); η_{y,r} is a homeomorphism, so η_{y,r}(S) is Borel for Borel S and ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} f dH^n = r^{−n}∫_S f(η_{y,r}(z)) dH^n(z) whenever either side is the integral of an integrable function (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, integral_smul_measure). Finally 0 ≤ J_g ≤ Λ^n everywhere and J_g is Borel (SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt): ‖Dg(a)‖ ≤ Λ (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz), and normDet(T) ≤ ‖T‖^n for every linear T : ℝ^n → E because normDet(T)·ω_n = H^n(T(B̄_1(0))) ≤ ‖T‖^n·ω_n (Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and (L1)). (3b) Density of Γ in M. For k ∈ ℕ let C_k := B̄_k(0) and ν_k := H^n⌞(M ∩ C_k), a finite Borel measure (H^n(M ∩ C_k) < ∞ by hypothesis). By the Besicovitch density theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for ν_k and Γ), for ν_k⌞Γ-a.e. y, ν_k(Γ ∩ B̄_r(y))/ν_k(B̄_r(y)) → 1 as r → 0⁺; since Γ ⊆ M and Γ, M, C_k are Borel, ν_k⌞Γ = H^n⌞(Γ ∩ C_k). Let N_1 be the union over k of the exceptional sets (so H^n(N_1) = 0), and call y ∈ Γ ∖ N_1 density-good; for such y and every k ≥ |y| + 1 the convergence holds. (3c) Smallness of M ∖ Γ. Let y = g(b) (b ∈ B) be density-good and k ≥ |y| + 1. For 0 < r < 1, B̄_r(y) ⊆ C_k; with a(r) := H^n(Γ ∩ B̄_r(y)) and z(r) := H^n((M ∖ Γ) ∩ B̄_r(y)) we have ν_k(Γ ∩ B̄_r(y)) = a(r) and ν_k(B̄_r(y)) = a(r) + z(r) < ∞; by (3b), for every ε ∈ (0, 1/2) there is r_ε ∈ (0, 1) with z(r) ≤ ε(a(r) + z(r)), hence z(r) ≤ 2εa(r), for 0 < r < r_ε. If a' ∈ B and g(a') ∈ B̄_r(y), then c|a' − b| ≤ |g(a') − g(b)| ≤ r; so Γ ∩ B̄_r(y) ⊆ g(B ∩ B̄_{r/c}(b)) and a(r) ≤ Λ^nω_nc^{−n}r^n (for every b ∈ B and r > 0). Thus z(r) ≤ 2εΛ^nω_nc^{−n}r^n for r < r_ε, i.e. r^{−n}z(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺. (3d) Good parameters. λ-a.e. b ∈ B satisfies (α) b is a density point of B (D), and (β) b is a Lebesgue point of J_g: ρ^{−n}∫_{B̄_ρ(b)}|J_g(a) − J_g(b)| dλ(a) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺ (Mathlib IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for the additive Haar measure λ and the bounded Borel, hence locally integrable, J_g). 4. (Pieces adapted to F.) For i, l ∈ ℕ put A_{i,l} := A_i ∩ g_i^{−1}(Z_l) (Borel, g_i being continuous), S_{i,l} := g_i(A_{i,l}) = g_i(A_i) ∩ Z_l (Borel) and Φ_{i,l} := F_l∘g_i : ℝ^n → ℝ^n (Lipschitz). For a ∈ A_{i,l}, g_i(a) ∈ Z_l, so F(g_i(a)) = F_l(g_i(a)) = Φ_{i,l}(a).
5. (Jacobian chain rule.) For all i, l and L^n-a.e. a ∈ A_{i,l}: J_{Φ_{i,l}}(a) = J*(g_i(a))·J_{g_i}(a). Indeed, by step 3 (A_{i,l} ⊆ A_i), L^n-a.e. a ∈ A_{i,l} satisfies T_{g_i(a)} = range Dg_i(a). Fix such an a and put x := g_i(a) ∈ Z_l ⊆ V_l, L := Dg_i(a) (injective, step 2(ii)) and A' := DF(x); F is C¹ on the open set Z ⊇ V_l, hence differentiable at x. Since F_l = F on the open set V_l ∋ x, F_l is differentiable at x with DF_l(x) = A' (maps that agree on a neighbourhood of x have the same derivative at x, Mathlib HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq, Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). By the chain rule, Φ_{i,l} = F_l∘g_i is differentiable at a with DΦ_{i,l}(a) = A'∘L. By (G), J_{Φ_{i,l}}(a) = normDet(A'∘L) = normDet(A'|_{range L})·normDet(L) = normDet(DF(x)|_{T_x})·J_{g_i}(a) = J*(x)·J_{g_i}(a).
6. (Carrier side.) M ∩ Z is the disjoint union of the H^n-null set N_0 and the Borel sets S_{i,l}. The restriction of H^n to the countable disjoint union ∪_{i,l} S_{i,l} is the sum of the restrictions (Mathlib Measure.restrict_iUnion), the lintegral against a sum of measures is the sum of the lintegrals for every [0, ∞]-valued integrand (lintegral_sum_measure), and N_0 contributes nothing; hence ∫_{M∩Z} J*h dH^n = Σ_{i,l} ∫_{S_{i,l}} J*h dH^n. For each (i, l), (A2) (φ := g_i, s := A_{i,l}, on which g_i is injective by 2(i), and κ := J*·h, for which no measurability is needed) and step 5 (the integrands agree L^n-a.e. on A_{i,l}; ofReal of a product of nonnegative reals is the product of the ofReal's) give ∫_{S_{i,l}} J*h dH^n = ∫_{A_{i,l}} J_{g_i}(a)J*(g_i(a))h(g_i(a)) dL^n(a) = ∫_{A_{i,l}} J_{Φ_{i,l}}(a)h(g_i(a)) dL^n(a).
7. (Fibre side and conclusion.) Fix y ∈ ℝ^n. Splitting the [0, ∞]-valued sum along the disjoint decomposition of step 6 (SimonGMT weightedAreaFiberSum_iUnion), Σ_{M∩Z}(y) = Σ_{N_0}(y) + Σ_{i,l} Σ_{S_{i,l}}(y). The first term vanishes unless y ∈ F(N_0), an L^n-null set by step 1(c). For each (i, l), a ↦ g_i(a) is a bijection from {a ∈ A_{i,l} : Φ_{i,l}(a) = y} onto {x ∈ S_{i,l} : F(x) = y} (g_i is injective on A_i, and F∘g_i = Φ_{i,l} on A_{i,l} by step 4), so Σ_{S_{i,l}}(y) = W_{i,l}(y) := Σ_{a ∈ A_{i,l}, Φ_{i,l}(a) = y} h(g_i(a)). Hence Σ_{M∩Z} = Σ_{i,l} W_{i,l} L^n-a.e. The weight h∘g_i is Borel (h Borel, g_i continuous), so (A1) (φ := Φ_{i,l}, s := A_{i,l}, w := h∘g_i, Y := ℝ^n, μHE[n] = L^n) shows that W_{i,l} is L^n-a.e. measurable with ∫ W_{i,l} dL^n = ∫_{A_{i,l}} J_{Φ_{i,l}}(a)h(g_i(a)) dL^n(a). Therefore Σ_{M∩Z} is L^n-a.e. measurable (a countable sum of a.e. measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions, AEMeasurable.ennreal_tsum, changed on a null set), and by lintegral_tsum and step 6, ∫ Σ_{M∩Z} dL^n = Σ_{i,l} ∫ W_{i,l} dL^n = Σ_{i,l} ∫_{A_{i,l}} J_{Φ_{i,l}}(a)h(g_i(a)) dL^n(a) = ∫_{M∩Z} J*h dH^n. ∎
proof_key_steps: Replace h by a Borel h̃ equal to it H^n-a.e. on M; the two sides change only on null sets, since C¹ maps send H^n-null subsets of Z to L^n-null sets.
Cover Z by countably many balls V_l on which F is Lipschitz; extend F|V_l to Lipschitz maps F_l on ℝ^P and disjointify into Borel sets Z_l.

Parametrization reduction: Rademacher's theorem and Mathlib's partition theorem decompose M, up to an H^n-null set, into disjoint Borel images g_i(A_i) of Lipschitz maps that are bi-Lipschitz with injective derivative on A_i.
Tangent identification: at L^n-a.e. a ∈ A_i the approximate tangent plane of M at g_i(a) is range Dg_i(a), by the density of g_i(A_i) in M, the injective area formula and a blow-up of g_i.

Chain rule: for a ∈ A_{i,l}, F_l = F on the open ball V_l ∋ g_i(a), so D(F_l∘g_i)(a) = DF(g_i(a))∘Dg_i(a); where T_{g_i(a)} = range Dg_i(a) (a.e.), normDet_comp and normDet_sq_eq_det_gram give J_{F_l∘g_i} = J*(g_i)·J_{g_i}.
Carrier side: by the injective area formula for g_i, ∫_{M∩Z} J*h dH^n = Σ_{i,l}∫_{A_{i,l}} J_{F_l∘g_i}·h∘g_i.
Fibre side: carrier fibre sums equal parameter fibre sums of F_l∘g_i off an L^n-null set, and the Euclidean Lipschitz area formula integrates them to the same series.

subproblems.title: Tangent cones of a 2-dimensional minimizing cone at points p ≠ 0 are integer multiples of planes through p
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ and every C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) that is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), has ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C) and is a cone (IsConeCurrent C), every p ∈ spt C with p ≠ 0, and every sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0: there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ, C' ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P), an orthonormal pair τ = (τ_1, τ_2) in ℝ^P and c ∈ ℤ such that blowUp C p λ_{φ(j)} ⇀ C' in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), the mass measures of these blow-ups converge to that of C' for all integer multiplicity representations (MassMeasuresConverge), p ∈ Q := span{τ_1, τ_2}, |c| ≥ 1, Θ²(μ_C, p) = |c| (HasMassDensity C p |c|), and C' = c[[Q]], i.e. C'(ω) = c∫_Q ω(x)(τ_1, τ_2) dH²(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟²(ℝ^P), where H² = μHE[2].

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent's step 4, case n − d = 2 (Simon 7.3.3(1), chapter-07.txt lines 497–510), needs the structure of 2-dimensional minimizing cones, which the book cites to [Whi82] without proof; this child supplies its first ingredient, the tangent cones of such a cone at points p ≠ 0. The argument is the book's own splitting argument for one translation direction (Lemma 3.5, lines 425–436, here in the form of the sibling result cone_splitting) followed by formula (10) of the proof of 3.3(2) (lines 547–555, the sibling result one_dim_cones) and the Constancy Theorem (Ch. 6, 2.34, the sibling child planar_constancy). Conventions. ℝ^P := Euclid P and B_ρ(x) is the open ball. For an integer multiplicity current A on an open set, μ_A denotes R.measure for any representation R of A (all representations have the same measure), M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W inside the domain of A, and spt A = {x in the domain : μ_A(B_ε(x)) > 0 for every ε > 0} (sibling results im_mass_measure (c), (a), (b), `Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure`); hence μ_A vanishes off spt A (Lindelöf). H² := μHE[2] and ω_2 := unitBallVolume 2. For a 2-dimensional subspace Q, H²⌞Q is the image of Lebesgue measure of ℝ² under a linear isometry (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`), so H²(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_2ρ² for y ∈ Q. η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y) (Lean `dilation y λ`) and blowUp A y λ = η_{y,λ#}A. For 2-currents, M_{η_{y,λ}(W)}(η_{y,λ#}A) = λ^{−2}M_W(A) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image`), η_{y,λ#}A has a representation with measure B ↦ λ^{−2}μ_A(η_{y,λ}^{−1}(B)) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_imrep`), and (η_{y,λ#}A)(ω) = λ^{−2}A(ω∘η_{y,λ}) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr`). Densities are unique: HasMassDensity A y θ and HasMassDensity A y θ' imply θ = θ' (both are ≥ 0 and ENNReal.ofReal is injective on [0, ∞)). (M) Monotonicity. Let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂C = 0. If P ≤ 1, every 2-covector on ℝ^P vanishes, so C = 0; hence P ≥ 2 whenever spt C ≠ ∅, and then we write P = 2 + k₀ to apply results stated in ℝ^{n+k}. ℝ^P = univ is an embedded C² P-dimensional submanifold (identity chart), closure ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P = ∅ and spt C ⊆ ℝ^P, so the sibling result monotonicity (`Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity`, with U = N = ℝ^P, n = 2, d = P) gives: ρ ↦ ρ^{−2}μ_C(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, ∞) for every y; Θ(y) := Θ²(μ_C, y) exists for every y (HasMassDensity C y Θ(y)) and Θ is upper semicontinuous; Θ ≥ 1 on spt C; hence μ_C(B_ρ(y)) ≥ ω_2ρ² for y ∈ spt C and ρ > 0; and Θ(y) = 0 for y ∉ spt C (a ball about y has μ_C-measure 0). (K) Cone facts. Let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be a cone (IsConeCurrent C). For λ > 0 the domain of blowUp C 0 λ is η_{0,λ}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P and currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(ω), so blowUp C 0 λ = C; mass scaling gives M_{λ^{−1}W}(C) = λ^{−2}M_W(C), i.e. μ_C(sW) = s²μ_C(W) for open W and s > 0, hence for all Borel sets (outer regularity of the locally finite measure μ_C). Consequently spt C is invariant under x ↦ sx (s > 0), Θ(sx) = Θ(x), μ_C(B_ρ(0)) = ρ²μ_C(B_1(0)) for ρ > 0, and μ_C({0}) = 0.
1. (Setup.) Since p ∈ spt C, P ≥ 2 by (M); write P = 2 + k₀. ℝ^P = univ is an embedded C² (2 + k₀)-dimensional submanifold, (closure univ ∖ univ) ∩ univ = ∅, C is minimizing in univ ∩ univ and spt C ⊆ univ ∩ univ. Since ∂C = 0, boundarySupport C = spt(∂C) = spt 0 = ∅ (the zero current vanishes on every test form, so every point lies in its zero region), hence p ∈ spt C ∖ boundarySupport C.
2. (A tangent cone.) density_and_tangent_cones (2) (`Submission.density_and_tangent_cones`, with n := 2, k := ℓ := k₀, U = N = ℝ^P, T := C, x := p), applied to the sequence (λ_j), gives a strictly increasing φ and C' ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) such that C_j := blowUp C p λ_{φ(j)} ⇀ C' (ConvergesWeakly), MassMeasuresConverge (C_j) C', C' is minimizing in ℝ^P (in particular integer multiplicity) and a cone (IsConeCurrent C'), and there is θ with HasMassDensity C p θ and HasMassDensity C' 0 θ. By (M) and uniqueness of densities, θ = Θ(p) ≥ 1.
3. (∂C' = 0.) Let β ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P). The domain of C_j is η_{p,λ}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P, so currentEval(C_j, dβ) = C_j(dβ); the blow-up commutes with the boundary (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_algebra` (iv)), so ∂C_j = blowUp (∂C) p λ_{φ(j)} = blowUp 0 p λ_{φ(j)} = 0 and C_j(dβ) = (∂C_j)(β) = 0. Hence C'(dβ) = lim_j currentEval(C_j, dβ) = 0, i.e. ∂C' = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C').
4. (Measures.) Let μ_j := μ_{C_j} and μ' := μ_{C'}. By the conventions, μ_j(B) = λ_{φ(j)}^{−2}μ_C(p + λ_{φ(j)}B) for Borel B, and MassMeasuresConverge gives ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ' for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Consequently, if s_j > 0 and s_j → 1, then s_j²∫ f(s_jy) dμ_j(y) → ∫ f dμ' for every such f: the functions f(s_j·) are supported in a fixed compact set K for large j and converge uniformly to f, and sup_j μ_j(K) < ∞ (take g ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with g ≥ 1_K; ∫ g dμ_j converges).
5. (μ' is invariant under translations along ℝp.) Fix t ∈ ℝ. For large j put λ := λ_{φ(j)}, s := 1 + λt > 0 and λ' := λ/s. For Borel B, by (K) (μ_C(sX) = s²μ_C(X)): μ_j(B + tp) = λ^{−2}μ_C(sp + λB) = λ^{−2}s²μ_C(p + λ'B), and λ^{−2}s²μ_C(p + λ'B) = s²·λ^{−2}μ_C(p + λ(s^{−1}B)) = s²μ_j(s^{−1}B). Hence, for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), ∫ f(y − tp) dμ_j(y) = s_j²∫ f(s_jy) dμ_j(y) with s_j := 1 + λ_{φ(j)}t → 1. Letting j → ∞ (step 4): ∫ f(y − tp) dμ'(y) = ∫ f dμ'. As f is arbitrary, μ'(B + tp) = μ'(B) for every Borel B (uniqueness in the Riesz representation of locally finite Borel measures on ℝ^P).
6. (Invariance of the density function.) C' is a cone, so μ'(sB) = s²μ'(B) by (K). For y ∈ ℝp, λ > 0, w ∈ ℝ^P and ρ > 0, step 5 gives M_{B_ρ(y+λw)}(C') = μ'(B_ρ(λw)) = λ²μ'(B_{ρ/λ}(w)) = λ²M_{B_{ρ/λ}(w)}(C'). So the density ratio of C' at y + λw and radius ρ equals that at w and radius ρ/λ, and HasMassDensity C' w θ' implies HasMassDensity C' (y + λw) θ' for every θ'.
7. (Splitting.) The sibling result cone_splitting (`Submission.dimred_invariant_cone_splitting`) applies to S := C', n := 2 and L := span{p} (dim L = 1 < 2): C' is minimizing in ℝ^P, ∂C' = 0 (step 3), and the density hypothesis is step 6. It gives S₀ ∈ 𝒟_{2−1}(ℝ^P), minimizing in ℝ^P, with ∂S₀ = 0, a cone, spt S₀ ⊆ p^⊥, and, for t ∈ ℝp and y ∈ p^⊥: t + y ∈ spt C' ⟺ y ∈ spt S₀, and HasMassDensity C' (t + y) θ' ⟺ HasMassDensity S₀ y θ'.
8. (The one-dimensional factor.) Transport S₀ along 2 − 1 = 1 (minimality, ∂S₀ = 0, the cone property, supports and densities are preserved) and apply the sibling result one_dim_cones (`Submission.dimred_one_dim_minimizing_cone`): there are e ∈ ℝ^P and m' ∈ ℕ with (m' > 0 ⇒ |e| = 1), spt S₀ ⊆ span{e}, and HasMassDensity S₀ y m' for every y ∈ span{e}. By step 7 with t = y = 0, HasMassDensity S₀ 0 θ; also HasMassDensity S₀ 0 m'; by uniqueness, m' = θ ≥ 1, so |e| = 1. For y ∈ span{e}, the positive density m' forces y ∈ spt S₀ (if y ∉ spt S₀, a ball about y lies in the zero region of S₀, every form admissible for M_{B_ρ(y)}(S₀) with small ρ is annihilated, so M_{B_ρ(y)}(S₀) = 0 and the density would be 0). Hence span{e} ⊆ spt S₀ ⊆ p^⊥, so e ⊥ p.
9. (spt C' lies in a plane through p.) Put τ_1 := p/|p|, τ_2 := e (an orthonormal pair) and Q := span{τ_1, τ_2}, so p ∈ Q and dim Q = 2. If x ∈ spt C', write x = t + y with t := ⟨x, τ_1⟩τ_1 ∈ ℝp and y := x − t ∈ p^⊥; by step 7, y ∈ spt S₀ ⊆ span{e}, so x ∈ Q. Thus spt C' ⊆ Q.
10. (Constancy.) The sibling child planar_constancy (`Submission.idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul`, with n := 2, V := ℝ^P, S := C', τ := (τ_1, τ_2)) applies: C' is integer multiplicity, ∂C' = 0, spt C' ⊆ Q, and ℝ^P ∩ Q = Q is connected. It gives c ∈ ℤ with C'(ω) = c∫_{ℝ^P∩Q} ω(x)(τ_1, τ_2) dH²(x) = c∫_Q ω(x)(τ_1, τ_2) dH²(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟²(ℝ^P), and M_W(C') = |c|·H²(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P. In particular M_{B_ρ(0)}(C') = |c|·ω_2ρ² for every ρ > 0, so HasMassDensity C' 0 |c|, and by uniqueness |c| = θ ≥ 1, i.e. 1 ≤ c.natAbs. By step 2, HasMassDensity C p |c|. Together with steps 2 and 9 (φ, C', τ, c) this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: P ≥ 2 and boundarySupport C = ∅; density_and_tangent_cones (2) at p gives a subsequential minimizing tangent cone C' with Θ_{C'}(0) = Θ(p) ≥ 1, and ∂C' = 0 because blow-ups of the cycle C are cycles.

Since C is a cone, a blow-up translated by tp is the blow-up at the rescaled scale λ/(1 + λt), dilated by 1 + λt; passing to the limit, μ_{C'} is invariant under translations along ℝp, so the density of C' is invariant under w ↦ y + λw (y ∈ ℝp, λ > 0).
cone_splitting with L = span{p} and one_dim_cones give a unit e ⊥ p with spt C' ⊆ Q := span{p, e} and Θ(p) = m' ∈ ℕ.

subproblems.title: A 2-dimensional minimizing cone is an integer multiple of a plane near any point p ≠ 0 around which its density is constant on the support
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, every C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) that is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), has ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C) and is a cone (IsConeCurrent C), every p ∈ spt C with p ≠ 0, every k ∈ ℕ and every δ > 0 such that Θ²(μ_C, y) = k (HasMassDensity C y k) for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(p): there are δ' > 0 and a 2-dimensional linear subspace Q of ℝ^P with p ∈ Q, spt C ∩ B_{δ'}(p) = Q ∩ B_{δ'}(p), and M_W(C) = k·H²(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ B_{δ'}(p), where H² = μHE[2].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2) (p : Euclid P) (k : ℕ) (δ : ℝ), IsMinimizingIn C univ → BoundaryVanishes C → IsConeCurrent C → p ∈ C.support → p ≠ 0 → 0 < δ → (∀ y ∈ C.support, y ∈ ball p δ → HasMassDensity C y k) → ∃ (δ' : ℝ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < δ' ∧ Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 ∧ p ∈ Q ∧ C.support ∩ ball p δ' = (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball p δ' ∧ ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ ball p δ' → C.massOn W = (k : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[2] (W ∩ (Q : Set (Euclid P)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent's step 4, case n − d = 2 (Simon 7.3.3(1), chapter-07.txt lines 497–510), uses that a 2-dimensional minimizing cone is a union of planes, citing [Whi82]; the book does not prove this. This child proves the local half of that structure: near a point where the density is constant on the support, the cone is a multiple of a plane. Regularity comes from the root result density_one_implies_regular (Simon 7.4.3, Allard's theorem) applied to C divided by its multiplicity. Planarity then follows from the first variation (Simon Ch. 4, 2.2–2.6) of the stationary cone along the rotation field of the tangent plane. Conventions. ℝ^P := Euclid P and B_ρ(x) is the open ball. For an integer multiplicity current A on an open set, μ_A denotes R.measure for any representation R of A (all representations have the same measure), M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W inside the domain of A, and spt A = {x in the domain : μ_A(B_ε(x)) > 0 for every ε > 0} (sibling results im_mass_measure (c), (a), (b), `Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure`); hence μ_A vanishes off spt A (Lindelöf). H² := μHE[2] and ω_2 := unitBallVolume 2. For a 2-dimensional subspace Q, H²⌞Q is the image of Lebesgue measure of ℝ² under a linear isometry (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`), so H²(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_2ρ² for y ∈ Q. η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y) (Lean `dilation y λ`) and blowUp A y λ = η_{y,λ#}A. For 2-currents, M_{η_{y,λ}(W)}(η_{y,λ#}A) = λ^{−2}M_W(A) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image`), η_{y,λ#}A has a representation with measure B ↦ λ^{−2}μ_A(η_{y,λ}^{−1}(B)) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_imrep`), and (η_{y,λ#}A)(ω) = λ^{−2}A(ω∘η_{y,λ}) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr`). Densities are unique: HasMassDensity A y θ and HasMassDensity A y θ' imply θ = θ' (both are ≥ 0 and ENNReal.ofReal is injective on [0, ∞)). (M) Monotonicity. Let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂C = 0. If P ≤ 1, every 2-covector on ℝ^P vanishes, so C = 0; hence P ≥ 2 whenever spt C ≠ ∅, and then we write P = 2 + k₀ to apply results stated in ℝ^{n+k}. ℝ^P = univ is an embedded C² P-dimensional submanifold (identity chart), closure ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P = ∅ and spt C ⊆ ℝ^P, so the sibling result monotonicity (`Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity`, with U = N = ℝ^P, n = 2, d = P) gives: ρ ↦ ρ^{−2}μ_C(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, ∞) for every y; Θ(y) := Θ²(μ_C, y) exists for every y (HasMassDensity C y Θ(y)) and Θ is upper semicontinuous; Θ ≥ 1 on spt C; hence μ_C(B_ρ(y)) ≥ ω_2ρ² for y ∈ spt C and ρ > 0; and Θ(y) = 0 for y ∉ spt C (a ball about y has μ_C-measure 0). (K) Cone facts. Let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be a cone (IsConeCurrent C). For λ > 0 the domain of blowUp C 0 λ is η_{0,λ}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P and currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(ω), so blowUp C 0 λ = C; mass scaling gives M_{λ^{−1}W}(C) = λ^{−2}M_W(C), i.e. μ_C(sW) = s²μ_C(W) for open W and s > 0, hence for all Borel sets (outer regularity of the locally finite measure μ_C). Consequently spt C is invariant under x ↦ sx (s > 0), Θ(sx) = Θ(x), μ_C(B_ρ(0)) = ρ²μ_C(B_1(0)) for ρ > 0, and μ_C({0}) = 0.
1. (Normalization.) Since p ∈ spt C, k = Θ(p) ≥ 1 by (M) and uniqueness of densities, and P ≥ 2; write P = 2 + k₀. Hypothesis and conclusion are invariant under replacing (p, δ, δ') by (sp, sδ, sδ') for s > 0: by (K), spt C, Θ and μ := μ_C transform accordingly, the subspace Q is unchanged, and μ(sW) = s²μ(W), H²(sW ∩ Q) = s²H²(W ∩ Q). Hence we may assume |p| = 1 and, decreasing δ, δ < 1/4. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) represent C, so μ = R.measure.
2. (θ = k on B_δ(p).) μ(K) < ∞ for compact K, so by the sibling child density_eq_multiplicity_ae (n := 2, U := ℝ^P), for H²-a.e. x ∈ M the ratio μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_2ρ²) tends to θ(x) ≥ 1. For such x, μ(B_ε(x)) > 0 for every ε > 0, so x ∈ spt C (im_mass_measure (b)); if moreover x ∈ B_δ(p), the hypothesis HasMassDensity C x k and uniqueness give θ(x) = k. So θ = k H²-a.e. on M ∩ B_δ(p).
3. (Dividing by k.) Put B := B_δ(p) and R_1 := (M ∩ B, 1, ξ). R_1 is an integer multiplicity triple in B: M ∩ B is Borel, countably 2-rectifiable and contained in B; the multiplicity 1 is measurable and positive; ∫_{M∩B∩K} 1 dH² ≤ μ(K) < ∞ for compact K; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H²⌞(M ∩ B); and at H²-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ B the approximate tangent space of M ∩ B at x equals that of M (accepted `Submission.dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff` with V := B, since (M ∖ (M ∩ B)) ∩ B = ∅), which ξ(x) orients. Let C_1 ∈ 𝒟_2(B) be the current represented by R_1 (accepted `Submission.dtc_imrep_current`). By step 2, for every ω ∈ 𝒟²(B), C(ιω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dH² = k∫_{M∩B} ξ(ω) dH² = k·C_1(ω), where ι regards ω as an element of 𝒟²(ℝ^P). Consequently M_W(C) = k·M_W(C_1) for every W ⊆ B (the admissible forms for M_W in ℝ^P and in B correspond, and ofReal(k·x) = k·ofReal(x)), and spt C ∩ B = spt C_1 (since k ≥ 1, an open set with compact closure in B lies in the zero region of C iff it lies in that of C_1).
4. (Properties of C_1.) (a) C_1 is integer multiplicity. (b) ∂C_1 = 0 in B: for β ∈ 𝒟¹(B), C_1(dβ) = k^{−1}C(ι dβ) = k^{−1}(∂C)(ιβ) = 0. (c) M_{B_ρ(p)}(C_1) = k^{−1}M_{B_ρ(p)}(C) for 0 < ρ ≤ δ, so HasMassDensity C_1 p 1. (d) p ∈ spt C_1 by step 3. (e) M_W(C_1) ≤ k^{−1}μ(B) < ∞ for every W ⊆ B. (f) C_1 is minimizing in B: let W ⊆ ℝ^P be open with closure W compact and contained in B, let S_1 ∈ 𝒟_2(B) be integer multiplicity with ∂S_1 = ∂C_1 (= 0), and let spt(S_1 − C_1) be compact and contained in B ∩ W. Then D := S_1 − C_1 is integer multiplicity (accepted `Submission.dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub`) with ∂D = 0. If R_D represents D, its measure vanishes off the compact set K := spt D ⊆ W (Lindelöf and im_mass_measure (b)), so H²(R_D.carrier ∖ K) = 0, and accepted `Submission.dtc_extend_by_zero` (U := ℝ^P, V := B) gives an integer multiplicity D̃ ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) whose restriction to B is D, with spt D̃ ⊆ K and ∂D̃ = 0. Define D_1 := D̃ and D_{i+1} := D_i − (0 − D̃), so that D_i(ω) = i·D̃(ω); all are integer multiplicity by dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub (0 is represented by the empty triple). Put S := C − (0 − D_k), so S(ω) = C(ω) + k·D̃(ω). Then S is integer multiplicity, ∂S = ∂C, spt(S − C) = spt D̃ ⊆ K is compact and contained in ℝ^P ∩ W, and W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P. Minimality of C gives M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S). For ω ∈ 𝒟²(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ B we have C(ω) = k·C_1(ω) and S(ω) = k·C_1(ω) + k·D(ω) = k·S_1(ω), ω being regarded as an element of 𝒟²(B). Hence M_W(C) = k·M_W(C_1), M_W(S) = k·M_W(S_1), and M_W(C_1) ≤ M_W(S_1).
5. (Regularity at p.) Apply density_one_implies_regular (`Submission.density_one_implies_regular`) with n := 2, k := ℓ := k₀, U := B, N := ℝ^P (identity chart; closure ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P = ∅), T_i := C_1, T := C_1 and y_i := y := p. Its hypotheses hold by step 4: C_1 is minimizing in B ∩ ℝ^P = B, the supports lie in ℝ^P, ∂C_1 = 0, the masses are uniformly bounded, the constant sequence converges, p ∈ ℝ^P ∩ B, HasMassDensity C_1 p 1, and p ∈ spt C_1. Hence p ∈ reg C_1: there are ρ > 0 with B_ρ(p) ⊆ B, m_1 ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, an embedded C¹ 2-dimensional submanifold M' ∋ p with an orientation ξ' (continuous on M', ξ'(y) = ±(α ↦ α(τ_1, τ_2)) for an orthonormal basis τ of T_yM'), H²(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ B_ρ(p), and C_1(ω) = m_1∫_{M'} ξ'(ω) dH² for ω ∈ 𝒟²(B) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_ρ(p). So C(ω) = k·m_1∫_{M'} ξ'(ω) dH² for every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B_ρ(p).
6. (Local structure.) Let ψ : V_0 → W_0 be a chart of M' at p as in IsEmbeddedSubmanifold: V_0 ⊆ ℝ² and W_0 ∋ p are open, ψ is C¹ and injective with injective derivative, ψ(V_0) = W_0 ∩ M', and ψ^{−1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W_0. Then ψ is a homeomorphism of V_0 onto W_0 ∩ M' and W_0 ∩ M' is closed in W_0 (a continuous injective map with this properness is a closed embedding). For x ∈ M' let T_xM' be the subspace with (T_xM' : Set) = tangentSpace M' x provided by IsOrientation; it is 2-dimensional, since ξ'(x) = ±(α ↦ α(τ_1, τ_2)) for an orthonormal basis (τ_1, τ_2) of it. For every chart point v ∈ V_0, Dψ(v)(ℝ²) ⊆ tangentSpace M' ψ(v) (use the curves t ↦ ψ(v + εtw) for w ∈ ℝ² and small ε > 0, and that the tangent space is a subspace), and both are 2-dimensional (Dψ(v) is injective), so Dψ(v)(ℝ²) = T_{ψ(v)}M'. Fix ρ' ∈ (0, 1/2) with B_{ρ'}(p) ⊆ W_0 ∩ B_ρ(p). (a) spt C ∩ B_{ρ'}(p) = M' ∩ B_{ρ'}(p). If x ∈ B_{ρ'}(p) ∖ M', some ball about x misses M' (relative closedness), C vanishes on the forms supported in it, and x ∉ spt C. If x ∈ M' ∩ B_{ρ'}(p), let α_x be a 2-covector with ξ'(x)(α_x) = 1 (ξ'(x) ≠ 0), choose ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ B_{ρ'}(p) and ξ'(y)(α_x) > 1/2 for y ∈ M' ∩ B_ε(x) (continuity of ξ'), and g ∈ C^∞_c(B_ε(x)) with g ≥ 0 and g(x) > 0. Then C(g·α_x) = k·m_1∫_{M'} g·ξ'(α_x) dH² ≠ 0, because the integrand is ≥ g/2 ≥ 0 and positive on M' ∩ {g > 0}, a set of positive H²-measure (it contains the image under ψ of a nonempty open subset of V_0, and Dψ is injective). So x ∈ spt C. (b) For every x ∈ M' the approximate tangent space of M' at x exists and equals the tangent space T_xM' (classical: near x, M' is the graph over T_xM' of a C¹ map u with u(0) = 0 and Du(0) = 0; η_{x,r}(M') is near 0 the graph of u_r(z) := r^{−1}u(rz), u_r → 0 in C¹ on compact sets, and the area formula gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dH² → ∫_{T_xM'} f dH² for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P)). Hence R' := (M' ∩ B_{ρ'}(p), |k·m_1|, sign(k·m_1)·ξ') is an integer multiplicity triple in B_{ρ'}(p) representing the restriction of C to B_{ρ'}(p), and so does (M ∩ B_{ρ'}(p), θ, ξ). By im_mass_measure (c), θ·H²⌞(M ∩ B_{ρ'}(p)) = |k·m_1|·H²⌞(M' ∩ B_{ρ'}(p)). Since θ ≥ 1 on M, H²((M Δ M') ∩ B_{ρ'}(p)) = 0, and for H²-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ B_{ρ'}(p): x ∈ M', θ(x) = |k·m_1|, and approxTangentPlane 2 M x = T_xM'. For the last point apply dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff to M ∩ M' ⊆ M and to M ∩ M' ⊆ M' with V := B_{ρ'}(p), and use the uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces.
7. (Coordinates.) Let Q := T_pM'. p ∈ Q: by (K), for small ε_0 > 0 the C¹ curve t ↦ (1 + ε_0t)p, t ∈ (−1, 1), lies in spt C ∩ B_{ρ'}(p) = M' ∩ B_{ρ'}(p) and has velocity ε_0p at t = 0, so ε_0p ∈ tangentSpace M' p = Q. Let e ∈ Q be a unit vector with e ⊥ p, let π be the orthogonal projection onto Q, and let A(x) := ⟨x, p⟩e − ⟨x, e⟩p. A is linear and antisymmetric (⟨Ax, y⟩ = −⟨x, Ay⟩), |Ax| = |πx|, Ap = e, and A = 0 on Q^⊥. On Ω := {x : ⟨x, p⟩ > 0} ⊇ B_{1/2}(p) put f(x) := arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, p⟩) ∈ (−π/2, π/2), so πx = |πx|(cos f(x)·p + sin f(x)·e). f is smooth on Ω, f(sx) = f(x) for s > 0, ∇f(x) = Ax/|πx|², ⟨∇f(x), x⟩ = 0 and f(p) = 0. Let F(x) := (|x|, f(x)) on Ω; then dF_p(p) = (1, 0) and dF_p(e) = (0, 1).
8. (Parametrization.) F∘ψ is C¹ near v_0 := ψ^{−1}(p), with invertible derivative dF_p∘Dψ(v_0), because Dψ(v_0) maps ℝ² onto T_pM' = Q (step 6) and dF_p restricted to Q is invertible (step 7). By the inverse function theorem there are s ∈ (0, 1/4) and an open V_1 ∋ v_0 such that F∘ψ maps V_1 C¹-diffeomorphically onto O := (1 − s, 1 + s) × (−s, s). Put G := ψ∘(F∘ψ|_{V_1})^{−1} : O → M'; it is C¹ and injective with injective derivative, and F∘G = id_O. N_1 := G(O) = ψ(V_1) is open in M', so N_1 = M' ∩ N for an open set N. Shrinking s we may assume N_1 ⊆ B_{ρ'/2}(p), and we replace N by N ∩ B_{ρ'}(p). Let γ(α) := G(1, α) for α ∈ (−s, s): γ is C¹, |γ(α)| = 1, f(γ(α)) = α, γ(0) = p. Claim: G(t, α) = tγ(α) on O. Fix α. The set I_α := {t ∈ (1 − s, 1 + s) : tγ(α) = G(t, α)} contains 1 and is closed in (1 − s, 1 + s) by continuity. It is open: if t ∈ I_α, then tγ(α) ∈ N; for t' close to t, t'γ(α) ∈ N, and t'γ(α) ∈ spt C by (K) (γ(α) ∈ M' ∩ B_{ρ'}(p) ⊆ spt C by 6(a)); so t'γ(α) ∈ spt C ∩ B_{ρ'}(p) ∩ N = M' ∩ N = G(O); since F(t'γ(α)) = (t', α) and F is injective on G(O), t'γ(α) = G(t', α). Hence I_α = (1 − s, 1 + s). Consequently T_{G(t,α)}M' = DG(t, α)(ℝ²) = span{∂_tG, ∂_αG} = span{γ(α), γ'(α)} (G = ψ∘(F∘ψ|_{V_1})^{−1} and step 6), where γ'(α) ≠ 0 and γ'(α) ⊥ γ(α).
9. (Conservation law.) minimizing_implies_stationary (`Submission.minimizing_implies_stationary`, with n := 2, k := ℓ := k₀, U = N = ℝ^P; spt C ⊆ ℝ^P and ∂C = 0) gives R.firstVariation X = 0 for every C¹ compactly supported X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (every vector is tangent to ℝ^P). Let λ ∈ C^∞_c((1 − s, 1 + s)) with λ ≥ 0, λ ≢ 0, let ψ_0 ∈ C¹_c((−s, s)), let K_0 := G(spt λ × spt ψ_0) (compact, ⊆ N_1 ⊆ N), and let ζ ∈ C^∞_c(N) with ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K_0. Put X(x) := ψ_0(f(x))λ(|x|)ζ(x)Ax, extended by 0 off N; X is C¹ with compact support in N ⊆ B_{ρ'}(p) ⊆ Ω. By 6(b), 0 = R.firstVariation X = |k·m_1|∫_{M'∩B_{ρ'}(p)} tr(P_{T_xM'}∘DX(x)) dH²(x). With g := (ψ_0∘f)·λ(|·|)·ζ we have DX = g·A + (Ax) ⊗ ∇g, where (v ⊗ w)(u) := ⟨w, u⟩v. For a 2-plane T with orthonormal basis (u_1, u_2), tr(P_T A) = Σ_i ⟨Au_i, u_i⟩ = 0 (A antisymmetric) and tr(P_T∘((Ax) ⊗ ∇g)) = ⟨P_T∇g, Ax⟩. Let x ∈ M' ∩ B_{ρ'}(p) with x ∈ spt ζ ⊆ N. Then x ∈ M' ∩ N = G(O) and x = G(F(x)), so ψ_0(f(x))λ(|x|) ≠ 0 forces x ∈ K_0, where ∇ζ(x) = 0. Moreover, for x = G(t, α) we have x/|x| = γ(α) ∈ T_xM', hence ⟨P_{T_xM'}(x/|x|), Ax⟩ = ⟨x/|x|, Ax⟩ = 0. So the λ'-term and the ∇ζ-term vanish, and 0 = ∫_{G(O)} ψ_0'(f(x))λ(|x|)⟨P_{T_xM'}∇f(x), Ax⟩ dH²(x) = ∫_{G(O)} ψ_0'(f(x))λ(|x|)·|P_{T_xM'}Ax|²/|πx|² dH²(x).
10. (Change of variables.) At x = G(t, α) let τ(α) := γ'(α)/|γ'(α)|. Then |P_{T_xM'}Ax|² = ⟨γ(α), Ax⟩² + ⟨τ(α), Ax⟩² = t²⟨τ(α), Aγ(α)⟩² (⟨y, Ay⟩ = 0), |πx|² = t²|πγ(α)|², and the area Jacobian of G is J_G(t, α) = |∂_tG ∧ ∂_αG| = |γ ∧ tγ'| = t|γ'(α)|. Differentiating f(γ(α)) = α gives ⟨Aγ, γ'⟩ = |πγ|², so ⟨τ, Aγ⟩ = |πγ|²/|γ'|. By the area formula for the injective C¹ map G with injective derivative (SimonGMT `integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative`, Chapter02/WeightedArea.lean; Simon Ch. 2, §3), 0 = ∫_O ψ_0'(α)λ(t)·t|πγ(α)|²/|γ'(α)| dt dα = (∫λ(t)t dt)·∫ψ_0'(α)κ(α) dα, where κ := |πγ|²/|γ'| is continuous on (−s, s). Since ∫λ(t)t dt > 0 and ψ_0 ∈ C¹_c((−s, s)) is arbitrary, ∫κψ_0' dα = 0 for every such ψ_0, i.e. κ has zero distributional derivative on (−s, s); transporting κ (extended by 0 off (−s, s)) along the volume-preserving linear isometry ℝ ≅ Euclid 1, this is exactly the hypothesis (for C¹ test functions with compact support in the image of (−s, s)) of SimonGMT `ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero` with n = 1, so κ is a.e. constant on (−s, s) and, being continuous, constant: κ ≡ κ(0) = |πp|²/|γ'(0)| = 1, because γ'(0) ∈ T_pM' ∩ p^⊥ = ℝe and ⟨∇f(p), γ'(0)⟩ = ⟨e, γ'(0)⟩ = 1 give γ'(0) = e.
11. (Planarity.) So |γ'| = |πγ|². By Cauchy–Schwarz, |πγ|² = ⟨Aγ, γ'⟩ ≤ |Aγ|·|γ'| = |πγ|³, so |πγ| ≥ 1 (πγ ≠ 0 on Ω), while |πγ| ≤ |γ| = 1. Hence γ(α) = πγ(α) ∈ Q, and since f(γ(α)) = α, γ(α) = cos α·p + sin α·e. Therefore G(O) = {t(cos α·p + sin α·e) : |t − 1| < s, |α| < s}, an open neighbourhood of p in Q. Choose δ' ∈ (0, δ) with B_{δ'}(p) ⊆ N and Q ∩ B_{δ'}(p) ⊆ G(O). Then spt C ∩ B_{δ'}(p) = M' ∩ N ∩ B_{δ'}(p) = G(O) ∩ B_{δ'}(p) = Q ∩ B_{δ'}(p), by 6(a) and N_1 = M' ∩ N.
12. (Mass.) Let C_{δ'} ∈ 𝒟_2(B_{δ'}(p)) be the restriction of C. It is integer multiplicity (accepted `Submission.dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity`), ∂C_{δ'} = 0, spt C_{δ'} = spt C ∩ B_{δ'}(p) = Q ∩ B_{δ'}(p) ⊆ Q, and B_{δ'}(p) ∩ Q is convex, hence connected and nonempty. The sibling child planar_constancy (`Submission.idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul`, with n := 2, V := B_{δ'}(p), τ := (p, e)) gives c ∈ ℤ with M_W(C_{δ'}) = |c|·H²(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ B_{δ'}(p), and M_W(C) = M_W(C_{δ'}) for such W (accepted `Submission.dtc_massOn_eq_of_agreeOn`). Comparing densities at p (k by hypothesis; |c|·H²(B_ρ(p) ∩ Q)/(ω_2ρ²) = |c| from the formula) gives |c| = k. Hence M_W(C) = k·H²(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ B_{δ'}(p). Together with step 11 (dim Q = 2, p ∈ Q), this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: θ = k a.e. near p (density_eq_multiplicity_ae), so C = k·C_1 on B_δ(p) with C_1 the multiplicity-one current of M ∩ B_δ(p); C_1 is an integer multiplicity minimizing cycle in B_δ(p) with density 1 at p (competitors scaled by k).
density_one_implies_regular gives p ∈ reg C_1: near p, spt C is an embedded C¹ surface M', C = k·m_1[[M']], and approximate tangent planes of the carrier are T_xM'.
The angle map F = (|x|, f) of the plane Q = T_pM' ∋ p parametrizes M' near p by G(t, α) = tγ(α), using that spt C is a cone.
Stationarity tested with X = ψ_0(f)λ(|x|)ζAx (A the rotation of Q) and the area formula give ∫ψ_0'κ = 0 with κ = |πγ|²/|γ'|, so κ ≡ 1 and γ ⊆ Q by Cauchy–Schwarz: spt C = Q near p.
planar_constancy on the restriction gives M_W(C) = k·H²(W ∩ Q) near p.

subproblems.title: Rigidity at the edge of a planar sector of a 2-dimensional minimizing cone: the density at the edge point equals the multiplicity of the sector
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), with ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C), and a cone (IsConeCurrent C). Let Q be a 2-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P, a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0 (so Q = span{a, e}), δ > 0 and k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 1. Assume a ∈ spt C and that for all t > 0 and φ ∈ (0, δ) the point y := t(cos φ·a + sin φ·e) satisfies Θ²(μ_C, y) = k (HasMassDensity C y k) and spt C ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ Q for some r > 0. Then Θ²(μ_C, a) = k (HasMassDensity C a k).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P) (δ : ℝ) (k : ℕ), IsMinimizingIn C univ → BoundaryVanishes C → IsConeCurrent C → Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → 0 < δ → 1 ≤ k → a ∈ C.support → (∀ t φ : ℝ, 0 < t → 0 < φ → φ < δ → HasMassDensity C (t • (Real.cos φ • a + Real.sin φ • e)) k ∧ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ C.support ∩ ball (t • (Real.cos φ • a + Real.sin φ • e)) r ⊆ (Q : Set (Euclid P))) → HasMassDensity C a k
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent's step 4, case n − d = 2 (Simon 7.3.3(1), chapter-07.txt lines 497–510), uses the classification of 2-dimensional minimizing cones, which the book cites to [Whi82] and does not prove. This child is the rigidity statement behind that classification. Its proof combines three ingredients: a conservation law of the stationary cone for the rotation field of Q (first variation, Simon Ch. 4, 2.2–2.6, via minimizing_implies_stationary), the weighted area formula on the rectifiable carrier (Simon Ch. 3, 2.4–2.5), which is the sibling child carrier_area_formula (`Submission.idtp_carrier_area_formula`), and the integrality of the multiplicity. Conventions. ℝ^P := Euclid P and B_ρ(x) is the open ball. For an integer multiplicity current A on an open set, μ_A denotes R.measure for any representation R of A (all representations have the same measure), M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W inside the domain of A, and spt A = {x in the domain : μ_A(B_ε(x)) > 0 for every ε > 0} (sibling results im_mass_measure (c), (a), (b), `Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure`); hence μ_A vanishes off spt A (Lindelöf). H² := μHE[2] and ω_2 := unitBallVolume 2. For a 2-dimensional subspace Q, H²⌞Q is the image of Lebesgue measure of ℝ² under a linear isometry (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`), so H²(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_2ρ² for y ∈ Q. η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y) (Lean `dilation y λ`) and blowUp A y λ = η_{y,λ#}A. For 2-currents, M_{η_{y,λ}(W)}(η_{y,λ#}A) = λ^{−2}M_W(A) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image`), η_{y,λ#}A has a representation with measure B ↦ λ^{−2}μ_A(η_{y,λ}^{−1}(B)) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_imrep`), and (η_{y,λ#}A)(ω) = λ^{−2}A(ω∘η_{y,λ}) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr`). Densities are unique: HasMassDensity A y θ and HasMassDensity A y θ' imply θ = θ' (both are ≥ 0 and ENNReal.ofReal is injective on [0, ∞)). (M) Monotonicity. Let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂C = 0. If P ≤ 1, every 2-covector on ℝ^P vanishes, so C = 0; hence P ≥ 2 whenever spt C ≠ ∅, and then we write P = 2 + k₀ to apply results stated in ℝ^{n+k}. ℝ^P = univ is an embedded C² P-dimensional submanifold (identity chart), closure ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P = ∅ and spt C ⊆ ℝ^P, so the sibling result monotonicity (`Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity`, with U = N = ℝ^P, n = 2, d = P) gives: ρ ↦ ρ^{−2}μ_C(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, ∞) for every y; Θ(y) := Θ²(μ_C, y) exists for every y (HasMassDensity C y Θ(y)) and Θ is upper semicontinuous; Θ ≥ 1 on spt C; hence μ_C(B_ρ(y)) ≥ ω_2ρ² for y ∈ spt C and ρ > 0; and Θ(y) = 0 for y ∉ spt C (a ball about y has μ_C-measure 0). (K) Cone facts. Let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be a cone (IsConeCurrent C). For λ > 0 the domain of blowUp C 0 λ is η_{0,λ}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P and currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(ω), so blowUp C 0 λ = C; mass scaling gives M_{λ^{−1}W}(C) = λ^{−2}M_W(C), i.e. μ_C(sW) = s²μ_C(W) for open W and s > 0, hence for all Borel sets (outer regularity of the locally finite measure μ_C). Consequently spt C is invariant under x ↦ sx (s > 0), Θ(sx) = Θ(x), μ_C(B_ρ(0)) = ρ²μ_C(B_1(0)) for ρ > 0, and μ_C({0}) = 0.
0. (Setup.) Since a ∈ spt C, P ≥ 2; write P = 2 + k₀. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) represent C and μ := μ_C = R.measure. Since a, e are orthonormal in the 2-dimensional Q, Q = span{a, e}. Let π be the orthogonal projection onto Q and q := id − π (q(a) = 0). By the sibling child cone_tangent_cone_planar (at a ≠ 0, a ∈ spt C), m := Θ(a) is a positive integer: it equals the integer |c| obtained in step 1 for every sequence (uniqueness of densities).
1. (Every tangent cone at a is ±m[[Q]].) Let λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0. cone_tangent_cone_planar gives a subsequence (not relabelled), c ∈ ℤ with |c| = m, an orthonormal pair τ' with a ∈ Q' := span τ', and C' with C_j := blowUp C a λ_j ⇀ C', C'(ω) = c∫_{Q'} ω(x)(τ') dH²(x), and MassMeasuresConverge (C_j) C'. C' is represented by (Q', m, sign(c)·(α ↦ α(τ'))) (SimonGMT `hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule` gives the orientation condition), so μ_{C'} = m·H²⌞Q'; and μ_{C_j}(B) = λ_j^{−2}μ(a + λ_jB). Vague convergence gives limsup_j μ_{C_j}(K) ≤ m·H²(Q' ∩ K) for compact K and liminf_j μ_{C_j}(V) ≥ m·H²(Q' ∩ V) for open V. Claim: Q' = Q. Let w = σa + ue with σ ∈ ℝ and u > 0. For large j, y_j := a + λ_jw = (1 + λ_jσ)a + λ_jue = t_j(cos φ_j·a + sin φ_j·e) with t_j := |y_j| > 0 and φ_j := arctan(λ_ju/(1 + λ_jσ)) ∈ (0, δ). By hypothesis Θ(y_j) = k ≥ 1, so y_j ∈ spt C and μ(B_r(y_j)) ≥ ω_2r² for every r > 0 (M). Hence μ_{C_j}(closedBall(w, r)) ≥ λ_j^{−2}μ(B_{λ_jr}(y_j)) ≥ ω_2r², so m·H²(Q' ∩ closedBall(w, r)) ≥ ω_2r² > 0 for every r > 0, and w ∈ Q' (Q' is closed). Thus {σa + ue : σ ∈ ℝ, u > 0} ⊆ Q', so Q = span{a, e} ⊆ Q' and Q' = Q.
2. (Cusp.) For every ε > 0 there is s_ε > 0 with |q(x)| ≤ ε|x − a| for every x ∈ spt C ∩ B_{s_ε}(a). Otherwise there are ε > 0 and x_j ∈ spt C with s_j := |x_j − a| → 0 and |q(x_j)| > εs_j. Put w_j := (x_j − a)/s_j, so |w_j| = 1 and |q(w_j)| > ε. By step 1 (λ_j := s_j) and compactness, along a subsequence w_j → w with |q(w)| ≥ ε and μ_{C_j} → m·H²⌞Q vaguely. As x_j ∈ spt C, μ_{C_j}(B_r(w_j)) ≥ ω_2r², and B_r(w_j) ⊆ closedBall(w, 2r) for large j, so m·H²(Q ∩ closedBall(w, 2r)) ≥ ω_2r² > 0 for every r > 0. Then w ∈ Q, contradicting |q(w)| ≥ ε.
3. (Coordinates.) Let A(x) := ⟨x, a⟩e − ⟨x, e⟩a. A is linear and antisymmetric (⟨Ax, y⟩ = −⟨x, Ay⟩), |Ax| = |πx|, Aa = e, A = 0 on Q^⊥, and tr(P_T A) = 0 for every orthogonal projection P_T. On Ω := {x : ⟨x, a⟩ > 0} put f(x) := arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩) ∈ (−π/2, π/2), so πx = |πx|(cos f(x)·a + sin f(x)·e). f is smooth on Ω, f(sx) = f(x) for s > 0, ∇f(x) = Ax/|πx|², ⟨∇f(x), x⟩ = 0, f(a) = 0 and ∇f(a) = e. Let F : ℝ^P → ℝ² (= Euclid 2) be F(x) := (|x|, arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩)), with the convention u/0 := 0 of Lean's division, so that F = (|·|, f) on Ω; F is Borel on ℝ^P (built from continuous maps and the measurable division) and C^∞ on the open set Ω (0 ∉ Ω). For s ∈ (0, 1/4] let Z_s := {x ∈ Ω : ||x| − 1| < s, |f(x)| < s, |q(x)| < s|x|} (open), and for 0 < s' ≤ s let Z_s(s') := {x ∈ Z_s : ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s'}.
4. (Localization.) Fix s_0 ∈ (0, 1/4] with 5s_0 < s_{1/20} (step 2), and let 0 < s' ≤ s ≤ s_0. (a) If x ∈ spt C ∩ Ω with ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s' and |q(x)| ≤ 2s|x|, then |q(x)| < (s'/4)|x| and |x − a| < 3s'. Indeed, η := |q(x)|/|x| ≤ 2s ≤ 1/2 and x̂ := x/|x| satisfy |πx̂| = (1 − η²)^{1/2} ≥ 1 − η². So |x̂ − a| ≤ |πx̂ − (cos f(x)·a + sin f(x)·e)| + |cos f(x)·a + sin f(x)·e − a| + |q(x̂)| ≤ η² + |f(x)| + η < s' + 1.5η, and |x − a| ≤ ||x| − 1| + |x̂ − a| < 2s' + 1.5η ≤ 5s < s_{1/20}. By step 2, (3/4)η ≤ η|x| = |q(x)| ≤ |x − a|/20 < (2s' + 1.5η)/20, so η < 4s'/27 < s'/4 and |x − a| < 2s' + 1.5s'/4 < 3s'. (b) Consequently spt C contains no x ∈ Ω with ||x| − 1| < s, |f(x)| < s and s|x|/2 ≤ |q(x)| ≤ 2s|x| (apply (a) with s' := s), and every x ∈ spt C ∩ Z_s(s') lies in B_{3s'}(a) ∩ Z_{s'} and satisfies |q(x)| < (s'/4)|x|.
5. (Stationarity and radial tangency.) minimizing_implies_stationary (`Submission.minimizing_implies_stationary`, with n := 2, k := ℓ := k₀, U = N = ℝ^P) gives R.firstVariation X = 0 for every C¹ compactly supported X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. By (K), μ(B_ρ(0)) = μ(B_1(0))·ρ² for ρ > 0 with μ(B_1(0)) < ∞, so accepted `Submission.dtc_cone_radial_tangency` gives x ∈ T_x := approxTangentPlane 2 M x for μ-a.e. x. Let E_0 be the set of x ∈ M with x = 0, or without an approximate tangent space of M at x, or such that ξ(x) does not orient T_x, or with x ∉ T_x; H²(E_0) = 0 (the field `orients` of R, μ(E_0) = 0 with θ ≥ 1 on M, and H²({0}) = 0). For x ∈ M ∖ E_0, ξ(x)(α) = ±α(u_1, u_2) for every orthonormal basis (u_1, u_2) of T_x. For x ∈ M ∖ E_0, T_x is 2-dimensional and contains x̂ := x/|x|; for a unit τ ∈ T_x with τ ⊥ x we have P_{T_x}(Ax) = ⟨τ, Ax⟩τ (since ⟨x̂, Ax⟩ = 0), so |P_{T_x}Ax| ≤ |Ax| = |πx| ≤ |x|. For x ∈ Ω put J(x) := |P_{T_x}Ax|/|πx|² and G(x) := |P_{T_x}Ax|²/|πx|² = J(x)·|P_{T_x}Ax| (T_x is defined for every x, and πx ≠ 0 on Ω); since |P_{T_x}Ax| ≤ |Ax| = |πx|, J ≤ 1/|πx| and 0 ≤ G ≤ 1 on Ω, and ⟨P_{T_x}∇f(x), Ax⟩ = ⟨∇f(x), P_{T_x}Ax⟩ = |P_{T_x}Ax|²/|πx|² = G(x) for x ∈ Ω (∇f(x) = Ax/|πx|², and P_{T_x} is an orthogonal projection). For x ∈ (M ∖ E_0) ∩ Ω and τ as above, J(x) = |⟨∇f(x), τ⟩| (⟨∇f(x), τ⟩ = ⟨Ax, τ⟩/|πx|² and P_{T_x}Ax = ⟨τ, Ax⟩τ); in the orthonormal basis (x̂, τ) of T_x, DF(x)x̂ = (⟨x̂, x̂⟩, ⟨∇f(x), x̂⟩) = (1, 0) and DF(x)τ = (⟨x̂, τ⟩, ⟨∇f(x), τ⟩) = (0, ⟨∇f(x), τ⟩), so J(x) is the Jacobian of F along T_x (step 7). Measurability: x ↦ P_{T_x} = (approxTangentPlane 2 M x).starProjection is a.e. strongly measurable for H²⌞M (accepted `Submission.imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm`), so x ↦ |P_{T_x}Ax| and, on Ω, J and G (continuous functions of P_{T_x} and x there) are a.e. measurable for H²⌞M, hence for μ ≪ H²⌞M.
6. (Conservation law.) Let s ∈ (0, s_0]. Fix χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ) with χ = 1 on (−∞, 1/4] and χ = 0 on [1, ∞), and put ζ(x) := χ(|q(x)|²/(s²|x|²)). ζ is smooth on ℝ^P ∖ {0}, ζ = 1 where |q(x)| ≤ s|x|/2 and ζ = 0 where |q(x)| ≥ s|x|. For λ ∈ C¹_c((1 − s, 1 + s)) and ψ ∈ C¹_c((−s, s)) let X(x) := ψ(f(x))λ(|x|)ζ(x)Ax for x ∈ Ω and X(x) := 0 otherwise. X is C¹ with compact support (C^∞ if λ and ψ are). Indeed, on the compact set {||x| − 1| ≤ s, |q(x)| ≤ s|x|} ⊇ spt(λ(|·|)ζ) we have |πx| ≥ (1 − s²)^{1/2}|x| > 0. Moreover ψ(f(x)) = 0 for x ∈ Ω near ∂Ω ∩ {πx ≠ 0} (there |f| → π/2 > s), so ψ∘f extends by 0 to a C¹ function on {πx ≠ 0}. With g := (ψ∘f)·λ(|·|)·ζ, DX = g·A + (Ax) ⊗ ∇g, where (v ⊗ w)(u) := ⟨w, u⟩v. For x ∈ M ∖ E_0 we have tr(P_{T_x}DX(x)) = ⟨P_{T_x}∇g(x), Ax⟩ and ∇g = ψ'(f)λζ∇f + (ψ∘f)ζλ'(|x|)x̂ + (ψ∘f)λ∇ζ. Three observations: ⟨P_{T_x}x̂, Ax⟩ = ⟨x̂, Ax⟩ = 0. ∇ζ(x) = 0 whenever x ∈ spt C and ψ(f(x))λ(|x|) ≠ 0 (by 4(b), either |q(x)| < s|x|/2, where ζ ≡ 1 nearby, or |q(x)| > 2s|x|, where ζ ≡ 0 nearby). If x ∈ spt C and ψ'(f(x))λ(|x|)ζ(x) ≠ 0, then x ∈ Z_s and ζ(x) = 1 (4(b)). Since μ-a.e. point lies in spt C ∩ (M ∖ E_0), R.firstVariation X = 0 becomes
(I) ∫_{Z_s} ψ'(f(x))λ(|x|)G(x) dμ(x) = 0.
7. (Fibres; the area formula on the carrier.) M is Borel and countably 2-rectifiable (fields of IMRep), μHE[2](M ∩ K) ≤ μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K (θ ≥ 1 on M; locallyIntegrable_mult with U = ℝ^P), Z_s is open, and F is C¹ on Z_s ⊆ Ω (step 3). So the sibling child carrier_area_formula (`Submission.idtp_carrier_area_formula`, with n := 2, M, Z := Z_s and F) applies: for every h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] that is a.e. measurable for H²⌞M, the fibre-sum function (t, α) ↦ Σ_{x∈M∩Z_s∩F^{−1}(t,α)} h(x) is L²-a.e. measurable on ℝ² and (AF) ∫_{ℝ²} Σ_{x∈M∩Z_s∩F^{−1}(t,α)} h(x) dt dα = ∫_{M∩Z_s} J*(x)h(x) dH²(x), where J*(x) := (det(⟨DF(x)u_i, DF(x)u_j⟩)_{i,j})^{1/2} and (u_i) is the standard orthonormal basis of T_x (Lebesgue measure on Euclid 2 is dt dα in the coordinates (t, α)). For x ∈ (M ∖ E_0) ∩ Z_s, J*(x) = J(x): T_x is 2-dimensional; the Gram determinant det(⟨DF(x)v_i, DF(x)v_j⟩) is the same for every orthonormal basis (v_1, v_2) of T_x (another orthonormal basis is vO with O orthogonal, which replaces the Gram matrix Γ by OᵀΓO, of determinant det(O)²det Γ = det Γ); and in the basis (x̂, τ) of step 5 the Gram matrix is diag(1, ⟨∇f(x), τ⟩²). As H²(E_0) = 0, J* = J H²-a.e. on M ∩ Z_s. Finally μ = θ·H²⌞M with θ Borel and finite, so ∫_{Z_s} φ dμ = ∫_{M∩Z_s} θφ dH² for every φ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (Mathlib lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul_non_measurable). For (t, α) ∈ O_s := (1 − s, 1 + s) × (−s, s) let X(t, α) := M ∩ Z_s ∩ F^{−1}(t, α), N(t, α) := Σ_{x∈X(t,α)} θ(x) ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞} and H(t, α) := Σ_{x∈X(t,α)} θ(x)·|P_{T_x}Ax|; since F(Z_s) ⊆ O_s, these sums vanish for (t, α) ∉ O_s, and N, H are L²-a.e. measurable by (AF) (h := θ, resp. h := θ·|P_{T_x}Ax|, a.e. measurable for H²⌞M by step 5). (a) With h := θ: ∫∫_{O_s} N = ∫_{M∩Z_s} Jθ dH² = ∫_{Z_s} J dμ ≤ ∫_{Z_s} |πx|^{−1} dμ ≤ 2μ(B_2(0)) < ∞ (J ≤ |πx|^{−1} on Z_s ⊆ Ω by step 5, and |πx| > (1 − s²)^{1/2}(1 − s) > 1/2 on Z_s). So N < ∞ a.e. on O_s, and H ≤ (1 + s)N (|P_{T_x}Ax| ≤ |x| < 1 + s on Z_s) is integrable on O_s. (b) With h := ∞·1_{E_0}, which vanishes H²⌞M-a.e. (H²(E_0) = 0) and is therefore a.e. measurable, the right side of (AF) is 0; so Σ_{x∈X(t,α)} h(x) = 0, i.e. X(t, α) ∩ E_0 = ∅, for a.e. (t, α). (c) Let b be a bounded Borel function on ℝ² with positive and negative parts b^±. Apply (AF) to h := θ·(b^±∘F)·|P_{T_x}Ax| (a.e. measurable for H²⌞M): on X(t, α) we have F ≡ (t, α), so the fibre sum is b^±(t, α)H(t, α); and J*h = θ·(b^±∘F)·G H²-a.e. on M ∩ Z_s (J* = J H²-a.e. there, and G = J·|P_{T_x}Ax| on Ω). Hence ∫∫_{O_s} b^±H dt dα = ∫_{Z_s} b^±(F(x))G(x) dμ(x) ≤ sup|b|·μ(Z_s) < ∞ (G ≤ 1), and, subtracting, ∫∫_{O_s} b(t, α)H(t, α) dt dα = ∫_{Z_s} b(F(x))G(x) dμ(x). In particular, by (I) (b(t, α) := ψ'(α)λ(t)), ∫∫_{O_s} ψ'(α)λ(t)H(t, α) dt dα = 0 for all λ, ψ as in step 6.
8. (H depends only on t.) By 7(c), ∫∫_{O_s} ψ'(α)λ(t)H(t, α) dt dα = 0 for all ψ ∈ C¹_c((−s, s)) and λ ∈ C¹_c((1 − s, 1 + s)) (step 6 allows C¹ test functions). subproblems.title: Two-dimensional minimizing cones have integer density at the vertex (classification of 2-dimensional minimizing cones proved)
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ and every C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P): if C is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C) and C is a cone (IsConeCurrent C), then there is m ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity C 0 m, i.e. Θ²(μ_C, 0) = m.
