Source: the parent's step 4, case n − d = 2, i.e. the book's proof of 7.3.3(1), chapter-07.txt lines 497–510: "S₀ a 2-dimensional area minimizing cone in ℝ^N. Then spt S₀ is contained in a finite union ∪_{i=1}^q P_i of 2-planes, with P_i ∩ P_j = {0} ∀ i ≠ j. (For a formal proof of this characterization of 2 dimensional area minimizing cones, see for example [Whi82].) In particular, since Θ^n(S, ·) is constant on P_i ∖ {0} (by the Constancy 2.34 of Ch. 6), we have that Θ^n(S, y) ∈ ℤ". Departure [D3]: the book does not prove the characterization. Its source [Whi82] is B. White's 1982 Princeton thesis, and S. X. Chang, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 1 (1988), Appendix A, pp. 761–762, only cites F. Morgan, Math. Ann. 261 (1982), for it. Steps 1–7 below prove the characterization from the sibling children cone_tangent_cone_planar, cone_constant_density_planar and cone_sector_endpoint_density; step 8 is the book's constancy argument. Conventions. ℝ^P := Euclid P and B_ρ(x) is the open ball. For an integer multiplicity current A on an open set, μ_A denotes R.measure for any representation R of A (all representations have the same measure), M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W inside the domain of A, and spt A = {x in the domain : μ_A(B_ε(x)) > 0 for every ε > 0} (sibling results im_mass_measure (c), (a), (b), `Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure`); hence μ_A vanishes off spt A (Lindelöf). H² := μHE[2] and ω_2 := unitBallVolume 2. For a 2-dimensional subspace Q, H²⌞Q is the image of Lebesgue measure of ℝ² under a linear isometry (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`), so H²(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_2ρ² for y ∈ Q. η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y) (Lean `dilation y λ`) and blowUp A y λ = η_{y,λ#}A. For 2-currents, M_{η_{y,λ}(W)}(η_{y,λ#}A) = λ^{−2}M_W(A) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image`), η_{y,λ#}A has a representation with measure B ↦ λ^{−2}μ_A(η_{y,λ}^{−1}(B)) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_imrep`), and (η_{y,λ#}A)(ω) = λ^{−2}A(ω∘η_{y,λ}) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_testForm_corr`). Densities are unique: HasMassDensity A y θ and HasMassDensity A y θ' imply θ = θ' (both are ≥ 0 and ENNReal.ofReal is injective on [0, ∞)). (M) Monotonicity. Let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂C = 0. If P ≤ 1, every 2-covector on ℝ^P vanishes, so C = 0; hence P ≥ 2 whenever spt C ≠ ∅, and then we write P = 2 + k₀ to apply results stated in ℝ^{n+k}. ℝ^P = univ is an embedded C² P-dimensional submanifold (identity chart), closure ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P = ∅ and spt C ⊆ ℝ^P, so the sibling result monotonicity (`Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity`, with U = N = ℝ^P, n = 2, d = P) gives: ρ ↦ ρ^{−2}μ_C(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, ∞) for every y; Θ(y) := Θ²(μ_C, y) exists for every y (HasMassDensity C y Θ(y)) and Θ is upper semicontinuous; Θ ≥ 1 on spt C; hence μ_C(B_ρ(y)) ≥ ω_2ρ² for y ∈ spt C and ρ > 0; and Θ(y) = 0 for y ∉ spt C (a ball about y has μ_C-measure 0). (K) Cone facts. Let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be a cone (IsConeCurrent C). For λ > 0 the domain of blowUp C 0 λ is η_{0,λ}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P and currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(ω), so blowUp C 0 λ = C; mass scaling gives M_{λ^{−1}W}(C) = λ^{−2}M_W(C), i.e. μ_C(sW) = s²μ_C(W) for open W and s > 0, hence for all Borel sets (outer regularity of the locally finite measure μ_C). Consequently spt C is invariant under x ↦ sx (s > 0), Θ(sx) = Θ(x), μ_C(B_ρ(0)) = ρ²μ_C(B_1(0)) for ρ > 0, and μ_C({0}) = 0.
0. (Trivial case.) If spt C = ∅, then μ := μ_C = 0 (μ vanishes off spt C), so M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = μ(B_ρ(0)) = 0 for every ρ > 0 and HasMassDensity C 0 0; take m := 0. Assume from now on spt C ≠ ∅, so P ≥ 2 by (M).
1. (Integer densities off the vertex.) By (M), Θ exists everywhere, is upper semicontinuous, Θ ≥ 1 on spt C and Θ = 0 off spt C. By (K), μ(sB) = s²μ(B), spt C, Θ are dilation invariant, and μ({0}) = 0. For p ∈ spt C ∖ {0}, the sibling child cone_tangent_cone_planar (with any sequence λ_j → 0⁺) gives HasMassDensity C p |c| with c ∈ ℤ, |c| ≥ 1; by uniqueness of densities, Θ(p) ∈ ℤ and Θ(p) ≥ 1.
2. (Points of locally constant density.) Let G := {p ∈ spt C ∖ {0} : there is δ > 0 with Θ(y) = Θ(p) for all y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(p)} and J := (spt C ∖ {0}) ∖ G. For p ∈ G, the sibling child cone_constant_density_planar (k := Θ(p)) gives δ_p > 0 (which we may take ≤ |p|/2 and ≤ the δ in the definition of G) and a 2-dimensional subspace Q_p ∋ p with spt C ∩ B_{δ_p}(p) = Q_p ∩ B_{δ_p}(p) and μ(W) = Θ(p)·H²(W ∩ Q_p) for open W ⊆ B_{δ_p}(p); hence μ⌞B_{δ_p}(p) = Θ(p)·H²⌞(Q_p ∩ B_{δ_p}(p)). Q_p is determined by p: two 2-dimensional subspaces through p that agree near p are equal. Every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_{δ_p}(p) lies in G with Θ(y) = Θ(p) and Q_y = Q_p, since spt C coincides with Q_p near y. By (K), G, J, Θ and Q are dilation invariant: sp ∈ G ⟺ p ∈ G, Q_{sp} = Q_p, and δ_{sp} may be taken to be sδ_p. Let S := {x : |x| = 1}, Σ := spt C ∩ S (compact), Σ_G := G ∩ S and Σ_J := J ∩ S. For p ∈ Σ_G let K_p := Q_p ∩ S, a great circle through p; then Σ ∩ B_{δ_p}(p) = K_p ∩ B_{δ_p}(p).
3. (Assume J ≠ ∅; a J-point of locally minimal density.) Suppose J ≠ ∅. By dilation invariance pick b' ∈ Σ_J, and fix r_1 ∈ (0, 1/2). Let m_0 := min{Θ(q) : q ∈ Σ_J ∩ B_{r_1/2}(b')} (a nonempty set of positive integers), attained at b ∈ Σ_J ∩ B_{r_1/2}(b'). By upper semicontinuity at b choose r ∈ (0, r_1/2 − |b − b'|) with Θ < m_0 + 1 on B_r(b). Since Θ is integer valued on spt C ∖ {0} and 0 ∉ B_r(b), Θ ≤ m_0 on spt C ∩ B_r(b). Every q ∈ Σ_J ∩ B_r(b) lies in B_{r_1/2}(b'), so Θ(q) ≥ m_0 by minimality, and hence Θ(q) = m_0. As b ∈ J, Θ is not constant on spt C ∩ B_ρ(b) for any ρ > 0; since Θ ≤ m_0 = Θ(b) there, for every ρ ∈ (0, r/2) some y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ρ(b) has Θ(y) < m_0. Then ŷ := y/|y| ∈ Σ ∩ B_{2ρ}(b) has Θ(ŷ) = Θ(y) < m_0, so ŷ ∉ Σ_J (as 2ρ < r), i.e. ŷ ∈ Σ_G. Call a point z ∈ Σ_G ∩ B_r(b) with Θ(z) < m_0 light: light points accumulate at b.
4. (Arcs.) Let r' := r/2. For a great circle K = Q_K ∩ S (Q_K a 2-dimensional subspace) put Λ_K := {z ∈ K ∩ Σ_G ∩ B_{r'}(b) : Q_z = Q_K}. Λ_K is relatively open in K: if z ∈ Λ_K, every z' ∈ K ∩ B_{δ_z}(z) ∩ B_{r'}(b) lies in K_z ∩ B_{δ_z}(z) = Σ ∩ B_{δ_z}(z) (K_z = K), hence in Σ_G with Q_{z'} = Q_z = Q_K (step 2). So every connected component A of Λ_K is an open arc of K, and not all of K, because the diameter of K is 2 > 2r'. Θ is constant on A, being locally constant on Σ_G (step 2) and A connected. If an endpoint a of A lies in B_{r'}(b), then a ∈ Σ_J. Indeed a ∈ Σ (Σ is closed). If a were in Σ_G, then Σ ∩ B_{δ_a}(a) = K_a ∩ B_{δ_a}(a) would contain the points of A near a, so K_a would contain an open arc of K, Q_a = Q_K, and a ∈ Λ_K — contradicting the maximality of the component A. Two such arcs (for possibly different K) are equal or disjoint: if z ∈ A ∩ A', then Q_K = Q_z = Q_{K'}, so K = K' and A, A' are components of the same Λ_K containing z. For a light point z ∈ B_{r'}(b) let A_z be the component of Λ_{K_z} containing z. It is a light arc: Θ ≡ Θ(z) < m_0 on A_z.
5. (Some light arc ends at a J-point inside B_{r'}(b).) Suppose no light arc A_z with z ∈ B_{r'/2}(b) has an endpoint in B_{r'}(b). Then each such arc has both endpoints on ∂B_{r'}(b) and passes through z ∈ B_{r'/2}(b). Its length is therefore at least r', since each of the two sub-arcs from z to an endpoint has length ≥ its chord ≥ r'/2. For such an arc A put Γ_A := {tw : w ∈ A, 1/2 < t < 3/2} ⊆ Q_K ∩ B_2(0); cones over distinct arcs are disjoint. By step 2 and dilation invariance, μ⌞B_{tδ_w}(tw) = Θ(w)·H²⌞(Q_K ∩ B_{tδ_w}(tw)) ≥ H²⌞(Q_K ∩ B_{tδ_w}(tw)) for w ∈ A and t > 0. Covering Γ_A by countably many such balls (Lindelöf) and disjointifying gives μ(Γ_A) ≥ H²(Γ_A) = ∫_{1/2}^{3/2} t·length(A) dt = length(A) ≥ r' (polar coordinates in Q_K). Hence there are at most μ(B_2(0))/r' < ∞ such arcs. By step 3 there are light points z_i → b with z_i ∈ B_{r'/2}(b), each lying on one of these finitely many arcs; so one arc A contains infinitely many z_i and b ∈ closure(A), which is A together with its two endpoints. The endpoints lie on ∂B_{r'}(b), so b ∈ A ⊆ Σ_G, contradicting b ∈ Σ_J. Hence there is a light arc A = A_z (z ∈ B_{r'/2}(b)) with an endpoint a ∈ B_{r'}(b). By step 4, a ∈ Σ_J, and by step 3, Θ(a) = m_0, while Θ ≡ k := Θ(z) < m_0 on A.
6. (Contradiction via the sector lemma.) Let Q := Q_K be the plane of A. Let e ∈ Q be the unit vector with e ⊥ a such that A = {cos φ·a + sin φ·e : 0 < φ < φ_A}, where φ_A ∈ (0, π) is the length of A. For t > 0 and φ ∈ (0, φ_A), y := t(cos φ·a + sin φ·e) = tw with w ∈ A ⊆ Σ_G. By dilation invariance Θ(y) = Θ(w) = k, i.e. HasMassDensity C y k, and spt C ∩ B_{tδ_w}(y) = t·(spt C ∩ B_{δ_w}(w)) = t·(Q ∩ B_{δ_w}(w)) ⊆ Q. Also a ∈ spt C, |a| = |e| = 1, ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, a, e ∈ Q, dim Q = 2 and k ≥ 1. The sibling child cone_sector_endpoint_density (δ := φ_A) gives HasMassDensity C a k, so Θ(a) = k < m_0 = Θ(a), a contradiction. Hence J = ∅.
7. (Classification.) Now Σ = Σ_G. For p ∈ Σ let O_p := {q ∈ K_p : q ∈ Σ, Q_q = Q_p}, so p ∈ O_p. O_p is relatively open in K_p, as in step 4. It is closed in K_p: if q_i ∈ O_p and q_i → q ∈ K_p, then q ∈ Σ = Σ_G and q_i ∈ B_{δ_q}(q) for large i; near q_i, Σ coincides with K_q (step 2 at q) and with K_p (as q_i ∈ O_p), so K_q and K_p share an open arc, Q_q = Q_p, and q ∈ O_p. Since K_p is connected, O_p = K_p: K_p ⊆ Σ and Q_q = Q_p for all q ∈ K_p. So two circles K_p, K_{p'} (p, p' ∈ Σ) are equal or disjoint (a common point q gives Q_p = Q_q = Q_{p'}), and Σ = ∪_{p∈Σ} K_p. Since Σ ∩ B_{δ_p}(p) = K_p ∩ B_{δ_p}(p), each ball B_{δ_p}(p) meets only the circle K_p among them. Finitely many such balls cover the compact set Σ, so Σ = K_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ K_q (q ≥ 1) with pairwise disjoint great circles K_i = P_i ∩ S, each P_i a 2-dimensional subspace, and P_i ∩ P_j = {0} for i ≠ j (a nonzero common vector would give a common point of K_i and K_j). By dilation invariance, spt C ∖ {0} = ∪_i (P_i ∖ {0}), so spt C ⊆ P_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ P_q.
8. (Constancy and the density at 0.) (a) For each i let V_i := ℝ^P ∖ ∪_{j≠i}P_j (open; V_i = ℝ^P if q = 1) and let C_i ∈ 𝒟_2(V_i) be the restriction of C to V_i (restrictDomain). C_i is integer multiplicity with mass measure μ⌞V_i (accepted `Submission.dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity`; a representation (M, θ, ξ) of C restricts to (M ∩ V_i, θ, ξ)), and ∂C_i = 0 in V_i (the boundary of the restriction is the restriction of the boundary). Also spt C_i = spt C ∩ V_i ⊆ P_i, and V_i ∩ P_i is connected and nonempty: it is P_i ∖ {0} if q ≥ 2 (as P_i ∩ P_j = {0}) and P_1 if q = 1. (b) The sibling child planar_constancy (`Submission.idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul`, with n := 2, V := V_i, S := C_i and τ an orthonormal basis of P_i) gives c_i ∈ ℤ with M_W(C_i) = |c_i|·H²(W ∩ P_i) for every open W ⊆ V_i. Hence the locally finite Borel measures μ⌞V_i and |c_i|·H²⌞(P_i ∩ V_i) agree on open subsets of V_i, and so on all Borel subsets of V_i (outer regularity). (c) μ(ℝ^P ∖ ∪_iP_i) = 0, since this open set misses spt C. Moreover μ({0}) = 0, and the sets P_i ∖ {0} ⊆ V_i are pairwise disjoint. So for every ρ > 0, M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = μ(B_ρ(0)) = Σ_i μ(B_ρ(0) ∩ (P_i ∖ {0})) = Σ_i |c_i|·H²(B_ρ(0) ∩ P_i) = (Σ_i |c_i|)·ω_2ρ². (d) With m := Σ_i |c_i| ∈ ℕ, M_{B_ρ(0)}(C)/(ω_2·ofReal(ρ²)) = m for every ρ > 0 (ω_2ρ² ∈ (0, ∞)), so the ratio tends to m as ρ ↓ 0 and HasMassDensity C 0 m. ∎

If the jump set J were nonempty, take a J-point b of locally minimal density m_0. Light arcs (density < m_0) accumulate at b, and by a finite-mass count one of them ends at a J-point a with Θ(a) = m_0.

subproblems.title: Simon 7.3.3(1): integer densities outside a set E with μH[n−3+α](E) = 0 (n ≥ 1)
subproblems.statement: For all n, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k and n ≥ 1, all sets U, N ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} and every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U): if U is open, N is an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N), (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, T is minimizing in U ∩ N (IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N)), spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T), then there is a set E ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} with μH[n − 3 + α](E) = 0 for every real α > 0 such that for every x ∈ U ∖ E there is an integer m with HasMassDensity T x m (Θ^n(μ_T, x) = m).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n k ℓ : ℕ), ℓ ≤ k → ∀ (U N : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), 1 ≤ n → IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N) → T.support ⊆ U ∩ N → BoundaryVanishes T → ∃ E : Set (Euclid (n + k)), (∀ α : ℝ, 0 < α → μH[(n : ℝ) - 3 + α] E = 0) ∧ ∀ x ∈ U \ E, ∃ m : ℤ, HasMassDensity T x m
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent steps 1–4 (Simon 7.3.3(1), Lemma 3.5 and the proof of 3.3(1), chapter-07.txt lines 367–510), with the parent's conventions; the classification of 2-dimensional minimizing cones, which the book cites to [Whi82] at lines 501–504, enters only through the sibling child two_dim_cone_density, where it is proved. P := n + k. For an integer multiplicity current A on an open set, μ_A denotes the measure R.measure of any representation R of A (all representations have the same measure), M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W inside the domain of A, and spt A = {x in the domain : μ_A(B_ε(x)) > 0 for every ε > 0} (sibling result im_mass_measure (c), (a), (b), `Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure`); Θ_A := Θ^n(μ_A, ·); ω_n := unitBallVolume n; η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y), so blowUp T y λ = η_{y,λ#}T ∈ 𝒟_n(η_{y,λ}(U)); H^n := μHE[n] = c_nμH[n] with c_n ∈ (0, ∞) (Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def`, `addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero`), so H^n and μH[n] have the same null sets. Mass scaling of blow-ups: M_{η_{y,λ}(W)}(η_{y,λ#}T) = λ^{−n}M_W(T) for λ > 0 (Simon 6.2.23; the accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image`). B_ρ(x) is the open ball.
1. (Densities.) Since n ≥ 1 and ∂T = 0, boundarySupport T = spt 0 = ∅. By the sibling result monotonicity (`Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity`, with P := n + k and d := n + ℓ, so 1 ≤ n ≤ d ≤ P), there is Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with HasMassDensity T x Θ(x) for x ∈ U (so Θ ≥ 0 on U), Θ upper semicontinuous on U, and Θ ≥ 1 on spt T; for each compact K ⊆ U there is Λ_K ≥ 0 such that e^{Λ_Kρ}ρ^{−n}μ_T(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, R) whenever closedBall y R ⊆ K (here M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) = μ_T(B_ρ(y)) because B_ρ(y) ⊆ U). Put E := {x ∈ U : Θ(x) ∉ ℤ}. For x ∈ U ∖ E, m := Θ(x) ∈ ℤ satisfies HasMassDensity T x m. It remains to prove μH[n − 3 + α](E) = 0 for every α > 0.
2. (Uniform density bounds.) Let K ⊆ U be compact with Θ < θ₁ on K, let θ₂ > θ₁, and let K'' ⊆ U be a compact set containing a 2σ₀-neighbourhood of K (σ₀ > 0). Then there is ρ₀ > 0 with μ_T(B_ρ(y)) ≤ θ₂ω_nρ^n for y ∈ K and ρ < ρ₀. Proof: for y ∈ K choose ρ_y ∈ (0, σ₀) with e^{Λρ_y}μ_T(B_{ρ_y}(y))/(ω_nρ_y^n) < θ₁ (Λ := Λ_{K''}; possible because the ratio tends to Θ(y) < θ₁ and e^{Λρ} → 1), and τ_y ∈ (0, ρ_y) with θ₁(ρ_y/(ρ_y − τ_y))^n ≤ θ₂. For |y' − y| < τ_y and ρ < ρ_y − τ_y, monotonicity at y' (closedBall y' ρ_y ⊆ K'') and B_{ρ_y−τ_y}(y') ⊆ B_{ρ_y}(y) give e^{Λρ}μ_T(B_ρ(y'))/(ω_nρ^n) ≤ e^{Λρ_y}μ_T(B_{ρ_y}(y))/(ω_n(ρ_y − τ_y)^n) < θ₁(ρ_y/(ρ_y − τ_y))^n ≤ θ₂. Cover K by finitely many B_{τ_y}(y) and let ρ₀ be the least ρ_y − τ_y.
3. (Densities of admissible zero-scale limits.) Let z ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0 with closedBall z (2r) ⊆ U, and θ₂ > 0, ρ₀ > 0 such that μ_T(B_ρ(y)) ≤ θ₂ω_nρ^n for y ∈ B_{3r/2}(z) and ρ < ρ₀. Let x_i ∈ B_r(z), λ_i > 0 with λ_i → 0, and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with blowUp T x_i λ_i ⇀ S (ConvergesWeakly), S minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂S = 0. Then: (a) M_{B_ρ(w)}(S) ≤ θ₂ω_nρ^n for all w ∈ ℝ^P and ρ > 0, hence θ ≤ θ₂ whenever HasMassDensity S w θ; (b) S is integer multiplicity, and if R_S = (M_S, θ_S, ξ_S) represents S, then for H^n-a.e. y ∈ M_S, HasMassDensity S y θ_S(y), where θ_S(y) is an integer ≥ 1. Proof of (a): fix w and ρ > 0. For all large i, |x_i + λ_iw − z| < r + λ_i|w| < 3r/2 and λ_iρ < min(ρ₀, r/2); then B_{λ_iρ}(x_i + λ_iw) ⊆ B_{2r}(z) ⊆ U, and B_ρ(w) = η_{x_i,λ_i}(B_{λ_iρ}(x_i + λ_iw)) lies in the domain η_{x_i,λ_i}(U) of blowUp T x_i λ_i. By mass scaling and im_mass_measure (a), M_{B_ρ(w)}(blowUp T x_i λ_i) = λ_i^{−n}M_{B_{λ_iρ}(x_i+λ_iw)}(T) = λ_i^{−n}μ_T(B_{λ_iρ}(x_i + λ_iw)) ≤ θ₂ω_nρ^n. The sibling child weak_limit_mass_bound (W := B_ρ(w), B := θ₂ω_nρ^n) gives M_{B_ρ(w)}(S) ≤ θ₂ω_nρ^n. If HasMassDensity S w θ, then ofReal(θ) = lim_{ρ↓0} M_{B_ρ(w)}(S)/(ω_nρ^n) ≤ θ₂, so θ ≤ θ₂. Proof of (b): S is integer multiplicity because it is minimizing. R_S is a representation on ℝ^P, so μ_S(K) = ∫_{M_S ∩ K} θ_S dH^n < ∞ for every compact K (local integrability of the multiplicity). By the sibling child density_eq_multiplicity_ae, for H^n-a.e. y ∈ ℝ^P, μ_S(B_ρ(y))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1_{M_S}(y)θ_S(y); for y ∈ M_S the limit is θ_S(y), a positive integer (θ_S is ℕ-valued and positive on M_S), and since M_{B_ρ(y)}(S) = μ_S(B_ρ(y)) (im_mass_measure (a)), HasMassDensity S y θ_S(y).
4. (μH[n − 3 + α](E) = 0, and E = ∅ if n ≤ 2.) For m ∈ ℕ, m ≥ 1, and β ∈ ℚ ∩ (0, 1/2) let U_{m,β} := {x ∈ U : Θ(x) < m − β} (open, since Θ is upper semicontinuous on the open set U) and E_{m,β} := {x ∈ U_{m,β} : Θ(x) ≥ m − 1 + β}. Every x ∈ E has Θ(x) ≥ 0 and Θ(x) ∉ ℤ, so Θ(x) ∈ (m − 1, m) for the integer m := ⌈Θ(x)⌉ ≥ 1, and then x ∈ E_{m,β} for every rational β with 0 < β < min(1/2, Θ(x) − m + 1, m − Θ(x)); so E = ∪_{m,β}E_{m,β}, a countable union. Fix (m, β) and x₀ ∈ U_{m,β}, and choose σ > 0 with closedBall x₀ (4σ) ⊆ U_{m,β}. By step 2 (K := closedBall x₀ (3σ/2), σ₀ := σ, K'' := closedBall x₀ (4σ), which contains the 2σ-neighbourhood of K, θ₁ := m − β, θ₂ := m − β/2; Θ < m − β on K'') there is ρ₀ > 0 with μ_T(B_ρ(y)) ≤ (m − β/2)ω_nρ^n for y ∈ B_{3σ/2}(x₀) and ρ < ρ₀. Apply the sibling result threshold_reduction (`Submission.dimred_threshold_reduction`) with z := x₀, r := σ (closedBall x₀ (2σ) ⊆ U), c := m − 1 + β > 0 and d₀ := n − 2 (natural subtraction). Call S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) an admissible zero-scale limit if blowUp T x_i λ_i ⇀ S (ConvergesWeakly) for some x_i ∈ B_σ(x₀) and λ_i > 0 with λ_i → 0, S is minimizing in ℝ^P and ∂S = 0; step 3 applies to every such S with z := x₀, r := σ, θ₂ := m − β/2. Hypothesis (H1) of threshold_reduction: let S be an admissible zero-scale limit, Q an n-dimensional subspace and c' ≥ c with HasMassDensity S y (1_Q(y)c') for every y ∈ ℝ^P; we derive a contradiction. Since 0 ∈ Q, HasMassDensity S 0 c', so c' ≤ m − β/2 by step 3(a). Let R_S = (M_S, θ_S, ξ_S) represent S and μ_S := R_S.measure. If μ_S = 0, then M_{B_ρ(0)}(S) = μ_S(B_ρ(0)) = 0 for every ρ > 0, so the density ratio of S at 0 vanishes identically and, by uniqueness of limits, ofReal(c') = 0, contradicting c' ≥ c > 0. Hence μ_S ≠ 0, so H^n(M_S) > 0 (μ_S = θ_S·H^n⌞M_S), and by step 3(b) there is y ∈ M_S with HasMassDensity S y θ_S(y), θ_S(y) an integer ≥ 1. By uniqueness of the limit (both values are ≥ 0 and ofReal is injective on [0, ∞)), θ_S(y) = 1_Q(y)c'; as θ_S(y) ≥ 1 > 0, y ∈ Q and c' = θ_S(y) ∈ ℤ. But m − 1 < m − 1 + β = c ≤ c' ≤ m − β/2 < m and no integer lies strictly between m − 1 and m: a contradiction. Hypothesis (H2): let S be an admissible zero-scale limit and L a linear subspace with d₀ ≤ d := dim L < n such that HasMassDensity S w θ implies HasMassDensity S (y + λw) θ for all y ∈ L, λ > 0, w and θ, and such that for every y ∈ ℝ^P: (there is θ ≥ c with HasMassDensity S y θ) ⟺ y ∈ L; we derive a contradiction. Since 0 ∈ L there is θ₀ ≥ c = m − 1 + β with HasMassDensity S 0 θ₀, and θ₀ ≤ m − β/2 by step 3(a). Since d₀ ≤ d < n, n − d ∈ {1, 2} (if n ≥ 2 then d₀ = n − 2 ≤ d ≤ n − 1; if n = 1 then d = 0). By the sibling result cone_splitting (`Submission.dimred_invariant_cone_splitting`; dim L < n, S minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂S = 0, and the density invariance just stated) there is S₀ ∈ 𝒟_{n−d}(ℝ^P), minimizing in ℝ^P, with ∂S₀ = 0 and a cone, such that HasMassDensity S (t + y) θ ⟺ HasMassDensity S₀ y θ for t ∈ L, y ∈ L^⊥; with t = y = 0, HasMassDensity S₀ 0 θ₀. Case n − d = 1: transport S₀ along the equality n − d = 1 to a current in 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) (minimality, ∂S₀ = 0, the cone property and HasMassDensity are preserved); the sibling result one_dim_cones (`Submission.dimred_one_dim_minimizing_cone`) gives e ∈ ℝ^P and m' ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity S₀ y m' for every y ∈ span{e}; with y = 0 and uniqueness of the density limit, θ₀ = m' ∈ ℤ. Case n − d = 2: transport S₀ along the equality n − d = 2 to a current in 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) (minimality, ∂S₀ = 0, the cone property and HasMassDensity are preserved); the sibling child two_dim_cone_density gives m'' ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity S₀ 0 m''; by uniqueness of the density limit, θ₀ = m'' ∈ ℤ. In both cases θ₀ ∈ ℤ and m − 1 < m − 1 + β ≤ θ₀ ≤ m − β/2 < m: a contradiction. Hence threshold_reduction gives: μH[d₀ − 1 + α](Z) = 0 for every α > 0, and Z = ∅ if d₀ = 0, where Z := {x ∈ B_σ(x₀) : HasMassDensity T x θ for some θ ≥ m − 1 + β} ⊇ E_{m,β} ∩ B_σ(x₀) (take θ := Θ(x)). If n ≥ 3 then d₀ = n − 2 ≥ 1 and (d₀ : ℝ) − 1 + α = n − 3 + α; if n ≤ 2 then d₀ = 0 and E_{m,β} ∩ B_σ(x₀) = ∅. By Lindelöf, countably many such balls B_σ(x₀) (x₀ ∈ U_{m,β}) cover U_{m,β} ⊇ E_{m,β}. Hence, by countable subadditivity, μH[n − 3 + α](E) = 0 for every α > 0 if n ≥ 3; and if n ≤ 2 then E = ∅, so μH[n − 3 + α](E) = 0 for every real α as well. Together with step 1 this proves the statement. ∎

E = ∪ E_{m,β}; per ball B_σ(x₀) apply threshold_reduction with c = m − 1 + β, d₀ = n − 2: (H1) fails by integrality of c'; (H2) fails by cone_splitting with one_dim_cones (n − d = 1) or two_dim_cone_density (n − d = 2).

2. (The flatness class for one ball.) Let 𝒞 := {(z, r) : z ∈ ℚ^P, r ∈ ℚ_{>0}, closedBall z (2r) ⊆ U}; the balls B_r(z), (z, r) ∈ 𝒞, cover U. Otherwise let b₀ be the barycenter of μ_{T'} and let 𝒯 be the class of pairs (S, U_S) arising as follows: x_i ∈ ℝ^P, λ_i ∈ (0, 1), |x_i| < 1 − λ_i, x_i → x, λ_i → λ ∈ [0, 1], U_S := η_{x,λ}(B_2(0)) if λ > 0 and U_S := ℝ^P if λ = 0, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U_S), and (η_{x_i,λ_i#}T')(ω) → S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U_S) (with tsupport ω eventually inside η_{x_i,λ_i}(B_2(0))). These members have the following properties. (Countable-test criterion for limits on ℝ^P approximated by currents whose domains exhaust ℝ^P.) Fix a countable family {ω_m} ⊆ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) such that for every R ∈ ℕ, every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0) and every ε > 0 there is m with tsupport ω_m ⊆ B_{R+1}(0) and sup_w |ω(w) − ω_m(w)| < ε (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm); for instance the forms χ_R·Σ_I p_I dx^I (R ∈ ℕ, I increasing multi-indices) with a fixed χ_R ∈ C^∞_c(B_{R+1}(0); [0, 1]) equal to 1 on closedBall 0 R and polynomials p_I with rational coefficients: approximate the coefficients of ω uniformly on closedBall 0 (R + 1) by such p_I (Weierstrass); since ω = 0 off B_R(0) and χ_R = 1 on closedBall 0 R, sup|ω − χ_R·p| ≤ sup_{closedBall 0 (R+1)}|ω − p|. Criterion (C): let V_k ⊆ ℝ^P be open, A_k ∈ 𝒟_n(V_k) and A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), and suppose that for every R ∈ ℕ there are k_R ∈ ℕ and Γ_R < ∞ with B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ V_k and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A_k) ≤ Γ_R for all k ≥ k_R, and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A) ≤ Γ_R. If A_k(ω_m) → A(ω_m) for every m (for k ≥ k_R these values are defined when tsupport ω_m ⊆ B_{R+1}(0)), then currentEval(A_k, ω) → A(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), i.e. A_k ⇀ A in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly). Proof: let tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0) and ε > 0, and choose ω_m as above. For k ≥ k_R, tsupport ω ⊆ V_k, so currentEval(A_k, ω) = A_k(ω); a test form β with tsupport β ⊆ W (W open) and sup|β| ≤ s satisfies |A'(β)| ≤ s·M_W(A') for every current A' (if s > 0, ±β/s is admissible for M_W(A')), so |A_k(ω) − A_k(ω_m)| ≤ Γ_Rε and |A(ω) − A(ω_m)| ≤ Γ_Rε; hence limsup_k |currentEval(A_k, ω) − A(ω)| ≤ 2Γ_Rε for every ε > 0. (The criterion is used only for limits on all of ℝ^P approximated by currents whose domains exhaust ℝ^P, and no metric for weak convergence on varying bounded domains is used: for a limit on a bounded domain, currentEval vanishes at the limit on a form whose support meets the boundary of the limit domain, although it need not vanish along the approximants. For example, in ℝ (n = P = 1) let λ_i ↑ 1, A_i := [[(−2/λ_i, 2/λ_i)]] ∈ 𝒟_1((−2/λ_i, 2/λ_i)) and A := [[(−2, 2)]] ∈ 𝒟_1((−2, 2)): A_i ⇀ A in (−2, 2) and μ_{A_i} → μ_A vaguely there, but for ω = g dx with spt g = [−2, 2] and ∫g > 0, currentEval(A_i, ω) = ∫g > 0 for every i while currentEval(A, ω) = 0.) (e) (Tangent cones of members.) Let (S, U_S) ∈ 𝒯 have parameters (x, λ), |y| < 1 and λ_k ↓ 0. Case λ > 0. Since η_{y,λ_k}∘η_{x,λ} = η_{x+λy,λλ_k}, η_{y,λ_k#}S = η_{x+λy,λλ_k#}T'; these are the restrictions to η_{x+λy,λλ_k}(B_2(0)) of the blow-ups blowUp T (z + r(x + λy)) (rλλ_k) of T at z + r(x + λy) ∈ B_r(z) (|x + λy| < 1 − λ + λ = 1) with scales rλλ_k → 0, and their domains η_{x+λy,λλ_k}(B_2(0)) ⊇ B_{(2−|x+λy|)/(λλ_k)}(0) exhaust ℝ^P. If z + r(x + λy) ∈ spt T, density_and_tangent_cones (2) (`Submission.density_and_tangent_cones`; boundarySupport T = ∅) gives a strictly increasing subsequence along which these blow-ups converge weakly in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), with convergence of the mass measures (MassMeasuresConverge), to a minimizing cone C; otherwise T vanishes on a ball around z + r(x + λy), the blow-ups vanish on every ball B_R(0) for large k, and C := 0. Because every compact set eventually lies in η_{x+λy,λλ_k}(B_2(0)), on which η_{y,λ_k#}S agrees with the blow-up of T, η_{y,λ_k#}S ⇀ C in ℝ^P and μ_{η_{y,λ_k#}S} → μ_C vaguely on ℝ^P along the subsequence; and C is a member with parameters (x + λy, 0) via the sequence x'_k := x + λy, λ'_k := λλ_k (k so large that λλ_k < 1 − |x + λy|): for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), tsupport ω ⊆ η_{x'_k,λ'_k}(B_2(0)) for large k and (η_{x'_k,λ'_k#}T')(ω) = currentEval(blowUp T (z + r(x + λy)) (rλλ_k), ω) → C(ω). If y ∈ spt S, density_and_tangent_cones (2) (U = N = ℝ^P, ℓ := k, the codimension P − n) gives a strictly increasing subsequence along which η_{y,λ_k#}S ⇀ C in ℝ^P and μ_{η_{y,λ_k#}S} → μ_C vaguely, C a minimizing cone; if y ∉ spt S, η_{y,λ_k#}S vanishes on every B_R(0) for large k and C := 0. Diagonal selection: pass to that subsequence, discard the k with λ_k ≥ 1 − |y|, and let (x_i, s_i) be a defining sequence of S (x_i → x, s_i ∈ (0, 1), s_i → 0, |x_i| < 1 − s_i, and η_{x_i,s_i#}T' → S in the sense of the definition of 𝒯; the letter s_i is used to distinguish these scales from the tangent scales λ_k). As η_{y,λ_k}∘η_{x_i,s_i} = η_{x_i+s_iy,s_iλ_k}, A_{k,i}(ω) = (η_{x_i,s_i#}T')(η_{y,λ_k}^#ω) whenever tsupport ω lies in the domain of A_{k,i}; since η_{y,λ_k}^#ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), the defining property of S gives, for fixed k and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P): tsupport ω lies in the domain of A_{k,i} for all large i, and A_{k,i}(ω) → S(η_{y,λ_k}^#ω) = (η_{y,λ_k#}S)(ω) as i → ∞. Choose i(1) < i(2) < ⋯ with s_{i(k)} < 1/k, |x_{i(k)} − x| < 1/k, and, for all m ≤ k, tsupport ω_m inside the domain of A_{k,i(k)} and |A_{k,i(k)}(ω_m) − (η_{y,λ_k#}S)(ω_m)| < 1/k (finitely many conditions, each holding for all large i). Then λ'_k ∈ (0, 1), λ'_k → 0, x'_k → x, and |x'_k| < 1 − s_{i(k)} + s_{i(k)}|y| ≤ 1 − s_{i(k)}λ_k = 1 − λ'_k (as |y| ≤ 1 − λ_k). By criterion (C) of (d), D_k ⇀ C in ℝ^P, i.e. for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), tsupport ω ⊆ η_{x'_k,λ'_k}(B_2(0)) for large k and (η_{x'_k,λ'_k#}T')(ω) → C(ω): C is a member with parameters (x, 0) = (x + λy, 0). In both cases, along the chosen strictly increasing subsequence, μ_{η_{y,λ_k#}S} → μ_C vaguely on ℝ^P and C is a cone. (f) A member with μ_S ≠ 0 and μ_S(λA) = λ^nμ_S(A) for all λ > 0, or with μ_S(ℝ^P) = ∞, has parameter 0 (members with λ > 0 have finite positive total mass, which a nonzero n-homogeneous measure cannot have). Density functions. Let e₁ be the unit vector of Euclid 1, H^n := μHE[n], and c_n := addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) ∈ ℝ≥0 (the scalar in Mathlib's definition μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n]); c_n ≠ 0 (addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero), so c_n ∈ (0, ∞) and H^n = c_n·μH[n]. Consider integer multiplicity currents A on open sets V_A ⊆ ℝ^P whose mass measure μ_A, extended by 0 outside V_A, is locally finite on ℝ^P; these include all members (finite total mass if λ > 0, μ_S(B_R(0)) ≤ c₂R^n if λ = 0, by (d)), all their rescalings η_{y,λ#}S, and the cones C of (e). For such A put ϑ_A(w) := limsup_{ρ↓0} μ_A(B_ρ(w))/(ω_nρ^n) when finite and 0 otherwise, and φ_A(w) := ϑ_A(w)·e₁; write ϑ_S, φ_S for members. Then: (i) ϑ_S = Θ_S on U_S (densities exist there by (a), (b)). (ii) ϑ_A is Borel. (iii) μ_A = ϑ_A·H^n as measures on ℝ^P: if R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A) represents A, then μ_A = R_A.measure is locally finite on ℝ^P, so by the sibling child density_eq_multiplicity_ae, for H^n-a.e. w ∈ ℝ^P, μ_A(B_ρ(w))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1_{M_A}(w)θ_A(w) < ∞; hence ϑ_A = 1_{M_A}θ_A H^n-a.e. and ϑ_A·H^n = θ_A·H^n⌞M_A = μ_A (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2) and Theorem 1.9; Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2)). (iv) (Normalization.) Since H^n = c_n·μH[n], (iii) gives μ_A = c_n·ϑ_A·μH[n], i.e. ∫ g·ϑ_A dμH[n] = c_n^{−1}·∫ g dμ_A for every bounded Borel g with compact support; in particular ∫_K ϑ_A dμH[n] = c_n^{−1}·μ_A(K) < ∞ for every compact K, so φ_A (Borel, ‖φ_A‖ = ϑ_A) is locally μH[n]-integrable. (H0) holds for members: if φ_S = φ_{S'} μH[n]-a.e., then ϑ_S = ϑ_{S'} H^n-a.e. (e₁ ≠ 0) (H^n and μH[n] have the same null sets), so μ_S = μ_{S'} by (iii), hence ϑ_S = ϑ_{S'} everywhere (ϑ is computed from μ) and φ_S = φ_{S'}. (v) (Correctly normalized weak pairings.) For every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ f·φ_A dμH[n] = (∫ f·ϑ_A dμH[n])·e₁ = c_n^{−1}(∫ f dμ_A)·e₁. Hence, for currents A_k, A as above, φ_{A_k} ⇀ φ_A in the sense of abstract_dimension_reduction (`Submission.abstract_dimension_reduction`) (∫ f·φ_{A_k} dμH[n] → ∫ f·φ_A dμH[n] for all such f) if and only if ∫ f dμ_{A_k} → ∫ f dμ_A for all such f, i.e. μ_{A_k} → μ_A vaguely on ℝ^P (the factor c_n^{−1} ∈ (0, ∞) and the vector e₁ are fixed). (vi) φ_{η_{y,λ#}A}(w) = φ_A(y + λw) for all w (μ_{η_{y,λ#}A} = λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ_A, by the accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_imrep`, so μ_{η_{y,λ#}A}(B_ρ(w)) = λ^{−n}μ_A(B_{λρ}(y + λw))). So F := {φ_S : (S, U_S) ∈ 𝒯} satisfies (H0) and local integrability by (iv), A.1 by (c) and (vi), and A.2 of abstract_dimension_reduction: given φ_S ∈ F, |y| < 1 and a strictly decreasing sequence λ_k > 0 with λ_k → 0, (e) gives a strictly increasing subsequence k_i and a member cone C with μ_{η_{y,λ_{k_i}#}S} → μ_C vaguely on ℝ^P, so φ_S(y + λ_{k_i}·) = φ_{η_{y,λ_{k_i}#}S} ⇀ φ_C ∈ F by (vi) and (v), and φ_C is homogeneous by (vii). Two further facts, (viii) and (ix), and a consequence (T3s): (viii) (domain recovery) for φ with 0 < I(φ) := ∫|φ| dH^n < ∞ (H^n = μHE[n], so I(φ_S) = μ_S(ℝ^P) by (iii)) and ∫|w||φ(w)| dH^n(w) < ∞ put λ(φ) := (m₀/I(φ))^{1/n}, b(φ) := I(φ)^{−1}∫w|φ(w)| dH^n(w), x(φ) := b₀ − λ(φ)b(φ) and U(φ) := B_{2/λ(φ)}(−x(φ)/λ(φ)); otherwise U(φ) := ℝ^P. (A.3(2).) For members and g(w) := y + λ'w (0 < λ' < 1, |y| ≤ 1 − λ'): spt(φ∘g) = g^{−1}(spt φ), U(φ∘g) = g^{−1}(U(φ)) by (viii), and R_j(φ∘g) = g^{−1}(R_j(φ)) because balls and slabs scale together (B_ρ(w) ↦ B_{λ'ρ}(g(w)), |q_Π(g(y) − g(w))| = λ'|q_Π(y − w)|); hence sing_j(φ∘g) = g^{−1}(sing_j φ). As B_2(0) ⊆ U_{S_k}, w_k ∈ spt S_k ∖ R_j(φ_{S_k}); pass to w_k → w, |w| ≤ 1; by (T3s), w ∈ spt S, and w ∉ sing_j φ_S (distance ≥ ε), w ∈ U_S, so w ∈ R_j(φ_S), witnessed by (ρ, Π) with s := sup_{y ∈ spt S ∩ B_ρ(w)}|q_Π(y − w)| < β_jρ. By abstract_dimension_reduction (`Submission.abstract_dimension_reduction`, with P := n + k, the same n, Q := 1, the family F of step 2 and sing := sing_j of step 3), (I) or (II) holds. Suppose (II) with d = n − 1: there are ψ = φ_S ∈ F and L with dim L = n − 1, sing_j ψ = L and ψ(y + λx) = ψ(x) for y ∈ L, λ > 0. By the sibling result cone_splitting (`Submission.dimred_invariant_cone_splitting`; dim L = n − 1 < n) there is S₀ ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P), minimizing, ∂S₀ = 0, a cone, with spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥ and t + y ∈ spt S ⟺ y ∈ spt S₀; by the sibling result one_dim_cones (`Submission.dimred_one_dim_minimizing_cone`, after transporting S₀ along n − (n − 1) = 1), spt S₀ ⊆ span{e} for some e. Hence spt S ⊆ L + span{e}, a subspace of dimension ≤ n, contained in some n-dimensional subspace Π''. Then U(ψ) = ℝ^P and every w ∈ spt ψ = spt S is witnessed in R_j(ψ) by (1, Π''), so sing_j ψ = ∅ ≠ L: a contradiction. Hence (I) holds or d ≤ n − 2, and since sing_j φ_{T'} ∩ B_1(0) = (spt T' ∩ B_1(0)) ∖ R_j(φ_{T'}) (B_1(0) ⊆ U(φ_{T'}) = B_2(0)), μH[n − 2 + α]((spt T' ∩ B_1(0)) ∖ R_j(φ_{T'})) = 0 for all α > 0 (n − 2 + α = d + (n − 2 − d + α)); for n = 1 case (II) is impossible, so this set is empty. Put G_{z,r} := spt T' ∩ B_1(0) ∩ ∩_j R_j(φ_{T'}) and F'_{z,r} := (spt T' ∩ B_1(0)) ∖ G_{z,r} = ∪_j((spt T' ∩ B_1(0)) ∖ R_j(φ_{T'})), and F_{z,r} := z + rF'_{z,r}. Then μH[n − 2 + α](F_{z,r}) = r^{n−2+α}μH[n − 2 + α](F'_{z,r}) = 0 for n ≥ 2 and α > 0, and F_{z,r} = ∅ for n = 1.
5. (Assembly.) Put F := ∪_{(z,r)∈𝒞}F_{z,r} (with F_{z,r} := ∅ when T' = 0). 𝒞 is countable, so μH[n − 2 + α](F) = 0 for every α > 0 by countable subadditivity (for n = 1 every F_{z,r} is empty, so F = ∅). Let x ∈ spt T ∖ F, β > 0 and R > 0. Choose j ≥ 1 with 2^{−j} ≤ β. As U is open, choose δ > 0 with closedBall x δ ⊆ U, a rational r with 0 < r < min(R/2, δ/3), and z ∈ ℚ^P with |z − x| < r; then closedBall z (2r) ⊆ closedBall x (3r) ⊆ U, so (z, r) ∈ 𝒞, and x ∈ B_r(z). Since x ∈ spt T ∩ B_r(z), μ_T(B_{2r}(z)) > 0 (im_mass_measure (b)), so T' ≠ 0, and w := (x − z)/r ∈ spt T' ∩ B_1(0), because spt T' = η_{z,r}(spt T) ∩ B_2(0) (the support of a blow-up is the dilated support, and restricting to the open set B_2(0) intersects the support with it). As x ∉ F_{z,r} = z + rF'_{z,r}, w ∉ F'_{z,r}, so w ∈ G_{z,r} ⊆ R_j(φ_{T'}): there are ρ_j > 0 and an n-dimensional subspace Π_j with B_{ρ_j}(w) ⊆ U(φ_{T'}) = B_2(0) and s_j := sup_{y ∈ spt φ_{T'} ∩ B_{ρ_j}(w)}|q_{Π_j}(y − w)| < 2^{−j}ρ_j. Since B_{ρ_j}(w) ⊆ B_2(0), ρ_j ≤ 2 − |w| ≤ 2 (if ρ_j > 2 − |w|, choose ε with 0 < ε < ρ_j − (2 − |w|) and a unit vector u with w = |w|u (any unit u if w = 0); the point w + (2 − |w| + ε)u lies in B_{ρ_j}(w) but has norm 2 + ε, so it is not in B_2(0)); note that ρ_j = 2 is possible when w = 0. Put ρ := rρ_j, so 0 < ρ ≤ 2r < R (as r < R/2), and Q := Π_j. Let y' ∈ spt T with |y' − x| < ρ and put y := (y' − z)/r. Then |y − w| = |y' − x|/r < ρ_j, so y ∈ B_{ρ_j}(w) ⊆ B_2(0) and y ∈ η_{z,r}(spt T) ∩ B_2(0) = spt T' = spt φ_{T'} ∩ U(φ_{T'}) (step 3: spt φ_S ∩ U_S = spt S for members, applied to the member T'). Hence |q_Q(y − w)| ≤ s_j < 2^{−j}ρ_j, and, as q_Q = id − p_Q is linear and y − w = (y' − x)/r, |(y' − x) − p_Q(y' − x)| = |q_Q(y' − x)| = r|q_Q(y − w)| < 2^{−j}rρ_j ≤ βρ. subproblems.title: Simon 7.3.3(2), corrected (13): a point flat at arbitrarily small scales has a tangent plane
subproblems.statement: For all n, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k and n ≥ 1, all sets U, N ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} and every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that U is open, N is an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N), (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, T is minimizing in U ∩ N (IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N)), spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T), and every x ∈ spt T: if x is flat at arbitrarily small scales, i.e. for every β > 0 and every R > 0 there are ρ with 0 < ρ < R and an n-dimensional linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} such that |(y − x) − p_Q(y − x)| < βρ for every y ∈ spt T with |y − x| < ρ (p_Q the orthogonal projection onto Q, Lean `Q.starProjection`), then T has a tangent plane at x (HasTangentPlaneAt T x: some tangent cone C of T at x, a ConvergesWeakly-limit of blowUp T x λ_j with λ_j > 0, λ_j → 0, has support an n-dimensional linear subspace).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n k ℓ : ℕ), ℓ ≤ k → ∀ (U N : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), 1 ≤ n → IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N) → T.support ⊆ U ∩ N → BoundaryVanishes T → ∀ x ∈ T.support, (∀ β : ℝ, 0 < β → ∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ρ < R ∧ ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid (n + k)), Module.finrank ℝ Q = n ∧ ∀ y ∈ T.support, dist y x < ρ → ‖(y - x) - Q.starProjection (y - x)‖ < β * ρ) → HasTangentPlaneAt T x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 8 (Simon 7.3.3(2), corrected (13): a point in ∩_j R_{β_j}(T) has a tangent plane), case ρ_∞ = 0; the hypothesis provides flatness at scales tending to 0, so the case ρ_∞ > 0 of the parent's step 8 does not arise. P := n + k. For an integer multiplicity current A on an open set, μ_A denotes the measure R.measure of any representation R of A (all representations have the same measure), M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W inside the domain of A, and spt A = {x in the domain : μ_A(B_ε(x)) > 0 for every ε > 0} (sibling result im_mass_measure (c), (a), (b), `Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure`); Θ_A := Θ^n(μ_A, ·); ω_n := unitBallVolume n; η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y), so blowUp T y λ = η_{y,λ#}T ∈ 𝒟_n(η_{y,λ}(U)); H^n := μHE[n] = c_nμH[n] with c_n ∈ (0, ∞) (Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def`, `addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero`), so H^n and μH[n] have the same null sets. Mass scaling of blow-ups: M_{η_{y,λ}(W)}(η_{y,λ#}T) = λ^{−n}M_W(T) for λ > 0 (Simon 6.2.23; the accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image`). B_ρ(x) is the open ball.
1. (Setup.) Since n ≥ 1 and ∂T = 0, boundarySupport T = spt 0 = ∅, so x ∈ spt T ∖ boundarySupport T. By the sibling result monotonicity (`Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity`, d := n + ℓ), every θ with HasMassDensity T x θ satisfies θ ≥ 1. For a subspace Q write p_Q for the orthogonal projection onto Q (Lean `Q.starProjection`) and q_Q := id − p_Q (the projection onto Q^⊥).
2. (Flat scales.) For each j ∈ ℕ apply the hypothesis with β := 2^{−j} and R := 1/(j + 1): there are ρ_j ∈ (0, 1/(j + 1)) and an n-dimensional subspace Q_j with |q_{Q_j}(y − x)| < 2^{−j}ρ_j for every y ∈ spt T with |y − x| < ρ_j.
3. (Convergence of the planes.) Choose orthonormal bases (v_{j,1}, …, v_{j,n}) of Q_j. By compactness of the unit sphere of ℝ^P, pass to a strictly increasing sequence j(i) along which v_{j(i),l} → v_l for l = 1, …, n; (v_1, …, v_n) is orthonormal; let Q := span{v_1, …, v_n}, so dim Q = n. Since p_{Q_j}(u) = Σ_l⟨u, v_{j,l}⟩v_{j,l}, |p_{Q_{j(i)}}(u) − p_Q(u)| ≤ 2|u|Σ_l|v_{j(i),l} − v_l| =: |u|κ_i with κ_i → 0; hence |q_{Q_{j(i)}}(u) − q_Q(u)| ≤ |u|κ_i.
4. (Tangent cone.) Apply density_and_tangent_cones (2) (`Submission.density_and_tangent_cones`) at x ∈ spt T ∖ boundarySupport T to the scales λ_i := ρ_{j(i)} > 0, λ_i → 0: there are a strictly increasing φ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with blowUp T x λ_{φ(i)} ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly), C minimizing in ℝ^P, C a cone (IsConeCurrent C), and θ with HasMassDensity T x θ and HasMassDensity C 0 θ; by (1), θ ≥ 1. Write σ_i := λ_{φ(i)} = ρ_{j(φ(i))}, Q'_i := Q_{j(φ(i))}, κ'_i := κ_{φ(i)} → 0; note j(φ(i)) ≥ i, so the tilt 2^{−j(φ(i))} ≤ 2^{−i}.
5. (∂C = 0.) Write n = n' + 1 and let ω ∈ 𝒟^{n'}(ℝ^P). The compact set tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω lies in the domain η_{x,σ_i}(U) of blowUp T x σ_i for all large i (x ∈ U, U open, σ_i → 0). The blow-up commutes with the boundary (η_{x,σ} is a proper affine diffeomorphism; Simon 6.2.23, GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward; accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_algebra`): ∂(blowUp T x σ_i) = blowUp (∂T) x σ_i = 0. Hence currentEval(blowUp T x σ_i, dω) = (blowUp T x σ_i)(dω) = ∂(blowUp T x σ_i)(ω) = 0 for large i, and C(dω) = lim_i currentEval(blowUp T x σ_i, dω) = 0. So ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C).
6. (Supports of the blow-ups.) spt(blowUp T x σ) = η_{x,σ}(spt T) (accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_algebra`; a test form is supported in an open W' iff its pullback by the affine diffeomorphism η_{x,σ} is supported in η_{x,σ}^{−1}(W'), so the zero regions correspond). Hence if u ∈ spt(blowUp T x σ_i) and |u| < 1, then y := x + σ_iu ∈ spt T with |y − x| < σ_i = ρ_{j(φ(i))}, and by (2), |q_{Q'_i}(u)| = σ_i^{−1}|q_{Q'_i}(y − x)| < 2^{−j(φ(i))} ≤ 2^{−i}.
7. (spt C ∩ B_1(0) ⊆ Q.) Let v ∈ ℝ^P with |v| < 1 and q_Q(v) ≠ 0; put δ := |q_Q(v)|/2 > 0 and δ' := min(δ, (1 − |v|)/2). For u ∈ B_{δ'}(v): |u| < 1, |q_Q(u)| ≥ 2δ − δ' ≥ δ, and |q_{Q'_i}(u)| ≥ δ − κ'_i > 2^{−i} for all large i. By (6), B_{δ'}(v) ∩ spt(blowUp T x σ_i) = ∅ for all large i. For such i, B_{δ'}(v) lies in the domain of blowUp T x σ_i (for large i), every test form supported in B_{δ'}(v) has support disjoint from spt(blowUp T x σ_i), so blowUp T x σ_i vanishes on it (a current vanishes on test forms whose support misses its support; accepted `Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support`), and therefore M_{B_{δ'}(v)}(blowUp T x σ_i) = 0. The sibling child weak_limit_mass_bound (W := B_{δ'}(v), B := 0) gives M_{B_{δ'}(v)}(C) = 0. Then C(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{δ'}(v) (if s := sup|ω| > 0, both ±ω/s are admissible for M_{B_{δ'}(v)}(C), so ±C(ω) ≤ 0). As B_{δ'}(v) is open with compact closure, it lies in the zero region of C, so v ∉ spt C.
8. (spt C ⊆ Q.) C is a cone: for λ > 0 and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), C(ω) = currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(η_{0,λ}^#ω), where tsupport η_{0,λ}^#ω = λ·tsupport ω. Hence if C vanishes on all test forms supported in an open set W', it vanishes on all test forms supported in λW' (apply the identity with λ^{−1}), so the zero region and the support of C are invariant under w ↦ λw (λ > 0). If v ∈ spt C, pick λ > 2|v|; then λ^{−1}v ∈ spt C ∩ B_1(0) ⊆ Q by (7), so v ∈ Q.
9. (Constancy.) C is integer multiplicity (being minimizing), ∂C = 0 by (5), spt C ⊆ Q by (8), and ℝ^P ∩ Q = Q is connected. By the sibling child planar_constancy (`Submission.idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul`, with V := ℝ^P and τ := (v_1, …, v_n), an orthonormal basis of Q) there is c ∈ ℤ with M_W(C) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P; put m := |c| ∈ ℕ. Since HasMassDensity C 0 θ with θ ≥ 1, M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) > 0 for small ρ > 0, so m ≥ 1.
10. (spt C = Q.) Let v ∈ Q and ε > 0: M_{B_ε(v)}(C) = m·H^n(B_ε(v) ∩ Q) = mω_nε^n > 0 (μHE[n] on Q is the isometric image of Lebesgue measure). If v ∉ spt C, then v lies in an open set W' with compact closure on which C vanishes; for ε small, B_ε(v) ⊆ W', so every form admissible for M_{B_ε(v)}(C) is supported in W' and M_{B_ε(v)}(C) = 0, a contradiction. Hence Q ⊆ spt C, and with (8), spt C = Q.
11. (Conclusion.) The scales lams i := σ_i > 0 tend to 0 and blowUp T x σ_i ⇀ C, so IsTangentConeAt T x C; and spt C = Q with dim Q = n. Hence HasTangentPlaneAt T x. ∎

density_and_tangent_cones (2) along these scales gives a minimizing cone C with blowUp T x ρ_j ⇀ C and density θ ≥ 1 at 0.
∂C = 0 because blow-ups of the cycle T are cycles.
The blow-ups' supports in B_1(0) lie in thinning slabs around Q_j; weak_limit_mass_bound gives spt C ∩ B_1(0) ⊆ Q, and the cone property gives spt C ⊆ Q.
